definition_zh: 意外的；偶然的；非故意的；附带性的
definition_en: happening by chance, not planned or intended
core_image: 两辆车相撞，谁也没想到
scene: 走廊上，两个学生转身时撞到一起，书撒了一地。 Their meeting was accidental, not planned.
sceneCN: 这里 accidental 是「偶然的」（第 1 个义项：因偶然发生）；句意为他们的相遇是偶然的，并非安排。

pos.zh: 形容词：意外的；偶然的；非故意的

derivatives.zh: 意外地；偶然地
事故；意外

senses.title: Happening by chance
senses.definition: happening without plan
senses.definitionCN: 没有计划地发生
senses.example: The fire was accidental, not planned.
senses.exampleCN: 那场火是意外，并非计划。
senses.why: Accident plus the adjective ending -al makes a word that describes what chance brings.
senses.whyCN: accident 加上形容词后缀 -al，构成描述「由偶然带来」的词。

senses.title: Not intended
senses.definition: done without meaning to do it
senses.definitionCN: 做的时候并无本意
senses.example: Her accidental remark hurt him.
senses.exampleCN: 她无意中的话伤了他。
senses.why: The word moved from events to people's words and acts, where chance means not on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从事件转到人的言行，此时「偶然」就是并非故意。

intro.en: The recorded history of accidental is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 accidental 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: The verb meant to happen or fall upon, and accident grew from it.
items.cn: 这个动词意为发生或落到身上，accident 由此而来。

items.en: The adjective ending -alis marked something that happens by chance.
items.cn: 形容词词尾 -alis 标记偶然发生的事物。

items.en: Old French carried the adjective into English.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词带进英语。

items.en: English used accidental for events that were not planned.
items.cn: 英语十五世纪用 accidental 指未计划的事件。

items.en: Today it also labels insurance damage and musical signs.
items.cn: 今天它也标记保险中的损坏与音乐记号。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: The adverb for something done by chance.
The noun for the unplanned event itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指未计划的事件本身。

entries.definition: A death caused by an unplanned event.
entries.definitionCN: 指由意外事件造成的死亡。

entries.definition: It stresses that no one meant to do it.
entries.definitionCN: 强调没有人有意做这件事。

entries.definition: It stresses the absence of a plan.
It names what happens without design.
entries.definitionCN: 指没有设计而发生的事。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: accident names an unplanned event, and -al makes the adjective: accidental means by chance.
normal.cn: accident 指未计划的事件，-al 构成形容词：accidental 就是偶然的。

normal.en: The same family also gives accidentally and accident.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 accidentally 与 accident。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase accidental damage.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「意外损坏」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of accidental in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 accidental 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: happening by chance, not planned or intended.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「意外的」时用它。

abstract.en: Picture two cars meeting by chance, with no plan behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象两辆车相撞，谁也没想到。

abstract.en: The same picture can be literal in one sentence and figurative in another.
abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

examples.en: The fire was accidental, not planned.
examples.cn: 那场火是意外，并非计划。

examples.en: Her accidental remark hurt him.
examples.cn: 她无意中的话伤了他。

examples.en: The damage was accidental.
examples.cn: 损坏是无意造成的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克西登特尔」——两辆车相撞谁也没想到：意外的

root: accidental 是 accident 的形容词形式。accident 来自拉丁语 accidere「发生、落到身上」，形容词词尾 -alis 标记偶然发生的事物，经古法语 accidentel 进入英语；今天它也标记保险中的损坏与音乐记号。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of accidental grows from one core image: two cars meeting by chance, with no plan behind it.
sensesIntro.cn: accidental 的各个义项都从同一个核心意象生长出来：两辆车相撞，谁也没想到。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two cars meeting by chance, with no plan behind it
core.cn: 核心意象：两辆车相撞，谁也没想到

branches.en: Sense 01 covers the most literal use: Happening by chance.
branches.cn: 义项 01 覆盖最字面的用法：偶然发生的。

branches.en: Sense 02 covers a wider everyday use: Not intended.
branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更宽泛的日常用法：非故意的。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 02 covers the two main uses: Happening by chance / Not intended.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 02 覆盖两个主要用法：偶然发生的、非故意的。

branches.en: Sense 01 covers a later use: Happening by chance.
branches.cn: 义项 01 覆盖再往后的一种用法：偶然发生的。

branches.en: Sense 02 covers the outer edge of the meaning: Not intended.
branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖意义的边缘：非故意的。

intro.en: accidental can be split into the parts below, which also connect it to common English patterns.
intro.cn: accidental 可以按下面的成分拆开，这些成分也把它与常见的英语构词方式连起来。

latinIntro.en: No recorded Latin cognate is securely attached to this word, so the list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠记录的拉丁同族词可以系在这个词上，因此该列表留空。

items.example: It is a form of ad- used before c.
items.exampleCN: 它是 ad- 在 c 前的变体。

items.example: It comes from cadere, meaning to fall.
It marks a plural noun in English.
It marks the past tense or a completed state.
items.exampleCN: 它标记过去时或已完成的状态。

items.example: It forms the present participle of a verb.
items.exampleCN: 它构成动词的现在分词。

items.example: It turns an adjective into an adverb.
It names the doer of an action.
items.exampleCN: 它指做某动作的人或物。

definition_zh: 公共的；公开的；公众的；公众；公开场合
definition_en: open for everyone to use or see, not hidden, and relating to the people as a whole; also the people themselves
core_image: 广场中央的一盏灯，四面都照得到，谁走近都能看清
scene: 广场的公告栏刚换上新的通知，路过的行人都停下来读那几行字。 The council made the plan public only after every resident had been told.
sceneCN: 这里 public 是「公开的、不再保密的」（第 2 个义项）；句意为在通知到每位居民之后，市政会才把方案公开。图中可辨识物件：公告栏、通知纸、驻足的路人。

derivatives.zh: public 加名词后缀 -ity，义为「宣传；曝光度」
public 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「公开地」
同出拉丁 publicare（使公开），义为「出版；发表」
来自拉丁 res publica（公共之事），义为「共和国」
public 加动词后缀 -ize，义为「宣传；使公开」

senses.title: Available for everyone to use
senses.definition: provided for all people to use, rather than for one person or a small group
senses.definitionCN: 供所有人使用，而不是供某个人或某个小圈子使用
senses.example: The public library stays open until nine.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公共图书馆开到晚上九点。
senses.why: The Latin adjective named what belonged to the people as a body, so a thing held in common rather than privately was called public.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁形容词本指「属于人民全体的」，因此凡由众人共有、不由私人占有的东西，就被称作 public。

senses.title: Known or seen by everyone
senses.definition: known or seen by everyone, with nothing kept secret
senses.definitionCN: 所有人都知道或看见的，没有任何部分被保密
senses.example: The report became public after the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 审判结束后，这份报告被公开了。
senses.why: If something belongs to all the people, hiding it from them makes no sense, so shared ownership slides into shared knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西既然属于全体人民，瞒着他们就没有道理，于是「共有」自然滑向「共知」。

senses.title: Relating to the people or the state
senses.definition: relating to the people as a whole, or to work done by the state on their behalf
senses.definitionCN: 与全体人民有关，或与以人民名义运作的国家事务有关
senses.example: Public spending on roads fell last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年用于道路的公共开支下降了。
senses.why: Money and decisions that concern everyone are handled in the name of all, so the adjective also marks what the state holds rather than what a private owner holds.
senses.whyCN: 涉及所有人的钱和决定都以全体之名来打理，所以这个词也用来标明由国家、而非私人掌握的事物。

senses.title: The people as a whole
senses.definition: the people of a country or community considered as one body, especially as readers, viewers or voters
senses.definitionCN: 把一个国家或社区的人看作一个整体，尤指读者、观众或选民
senses.example: The gallery opened its doors to the public at ten.
senses.exampleCN: 美术馆十点向公众开门。
senses.why: The adjective was used so often with a noun left unsaid that it became a noun itself, naming the crowd a place is open to.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词常与一个被省略的名词连用，久而久之自己变成了名词，专指场所向其开放的那群人。

senses.title: An open setting where others can see and hear
senses.definition: an open place or setting where other people can see and hear what happens
senses.definitionCN: 一个开放的场景，别人能看见、听见发生的事
senses.example: She has never sung in public before.
senses.exampleCN: 她以前从未在公开场合唱过歌。
senses.why: A public place is one open to all, so the noun in the phrase in public names that open setting itself, in contrast with a private room.
senses.whyCN: public 的地方就是对所有人开放的地方，因此 in public 中的名词正指这个开放场景本身，与私密房间相对。

intro.en: Public came into English through French from Latin publicus, an adjective built on populus, the people; the noun use is a later English development.
intro.cn: public 经法语从拉丁语 publicus 进入英语，publicus 是由 populus（人民）构成的形容词；名词用法是英语后来发展出来的。

items.en: Populus meant the people as a body, and it is the base from which publicus was formed.
items.cn: populus 意为作为整体的人民，是构成 publicus 的基础。

items.en: Publicus meant belonging to the people or the state; an older form poplicus is recorded, which shows the link with populus.
items.cn: publicus 意为「属于人民或国家的」；文献中还有更早的形式 poplicus，可见它与 populus 的联系。

items.en: Old French took the adjective as public with the same sense of open and common, and passed it into English in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词写作 public，保留「开放的、共有的」意思，十五世纪传入英语。

items.en: English began using public as a noun for the people, first in phrases such as in public and then standing alone with the definite article.
items.cn: 英语开始把 public 用作指人民的名词，先出现在 in public 这类短语中，后来能单独与定冠词连用。

items.en: Modern English builds public transport, public health and public opinion, and pairs public with private as opposite poles.
items.cn: 现代英语构成 public transport、public health、public opinion 等说法，并把 public 与 private 配成对立的两极。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers English words built on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for what is shared or open.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一拉丁词干上的英语词；近义组收表示「共有、开放」的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for attention from the media, formed with -ity.
entries.definitionCN: 由 -ity 构成、指媒体关注的名词。

entries.definition: To make a text available to the public, from Latin publicare.
entries.definitionCN: 使文字向公众发行，出自拉丁语 publicare。

entries.definition: A state whose head is elected, from Latin res publica, the public thing.
entries.definitionCN: 元首经选举产生的国家，出自拉丁语 res publica（公共之事）。

entries.definition: A British pub keeper; the Latin word meant a tax farmer.
entries.definitionCN: 英国的酒馆老板；这个拉丁词原指包税人。

entries.definition: Shared by a group rather than owned by one person.
entries.definitionCN: 由群体共用，而非一人独占的。

entries.definition: Done or held by all the members of a group together.
entries.definitionCN: 由群体全体成员共同做出或持有的。

entries.definition: Not closed or hidden, and free for anyone to enter.
entries.definitionCN: 未关闭、未隐藏，任何人都可进入的。

entries.definition: Relating to a town and the duties of the people who live there.
entries.definitionCN: 与城镇及居民义务有关的。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin adjective for what belongs to the people, and English later let it stand alone as a noun for those people.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词本是表示「属于人民」的拉丁形容词，英语后来让它单独作名词，指那些人民。

normal.en: Public came through French from Latin publicus, an adjective built on populus, the people.
normal.cn: public 经法语来自拉丁 publicus，而 publicus 是由 populus（人民）构成的形容词。

normal.en: The noun public is the adjective standing alone, naming the people a place is open to.
normal.cn: 名词 public 就是单独站立的形容词，指场所向其开放的那群人。

normal.en: Public and private form a pair: one belongs to all, the other belongs to one person or one household.
normal.cn: public 与 private 成对：前者属于所有人，后者属于一个人或一个家庭。

normal.en: Publicity is public with -ity and publicly is public with -ly, and both keep the same idea of openness.
normal.cn: publicity 是 public 加 -ity，publicly 是 public 加 -ly，两者都保留着同一层「开放」的意思。

normal.en: Publish comes from Latin publicare, to make public, which is why publishing is always an act aimed at readers.
normal.cn: publish 出自拉丁 publicare（使公开），所以出版始终是朝着读者做出的动作。

abstract.en: The word is a lamp in the middle of a square: no side of the square is darker than another.
abstract.cn: 这个词就是广场中央的一盏灯：广场的任何一边都不会比另一边更暗。

abstract.en: A matter turns public when the cost of hiding it grows higher than the cost of showing it.
abstract.cn: 一件事之所以转为公开，往往是因为隐瞒的代价高过了示人的代价。

abstract.en: English keeps one word for shared ownership, shared knowledge and shared space, as if all three were one openness.
abstract.cn: 英语用同一个词涵盖共有、共知与共用空间，仿佛这三者本就是同一种开放。

examples.en: The park is public land, so anyone may walk there.
examples.cn: 这座公园是公共土地，任何人都可以进去散步。

examples.en: Details of the deal were made public yesterday.
examples.cn: 交易的细节昨天被公开了。

examples.en: He rarely speaks in public.
examples.cn: 他很少在公开场合讲话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「帕布立克」——广场上人人都立着看得见，记住 public 是公共的、公开的。

root: 拉丁语 populus（人民）→ publicus（属于人民的）→ 古法语 public → 英语 public；加 -ity 得 publicity，加 -ly 得 publicly，词义核心都是「向所有人开放」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what belongs to all the people; the senses divide into shared use, shared knowledge, state affairs, the people themselves, and the open setting.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「属于全体人民的东西」；义项由此分为共同使用、共同知晓、国家事务、人民本身，以及开放的场景。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp at the centre of a square, lighting every side of it evenly.
core.cn: 核心意象：广场正中的一盏灯，把四面照得一样亮。

branches.en: a library door with no ticket desk
branches.cn: 没有售票台的图书馆大门

branches.en: a lamp that leaves no corner dark
branches.cn: 一盏不留下暗角的灯

branches.en: a road paid for out of common funds
branches.cn: 用公共资金修起来的路

branches.en: a crowd waiting for the gallery to open
branches.cn: 等着美术馆开门的人群

branches.en: a first song sung before strangers
branches.cn: 第一次在陌生人面前唱歌

intro.en: The word is held together by the Latin noun for the people, the adjective built on it, and the English endings -ity and -ly that turn it into a noun and an adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示人民的拉丁名词、由它构成的形容词，以及把它变成名词与副词的英语后缀 -ity、-ly 共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 公开性；公众所知的状态

definition_zh: 飞机；平面；层面；刨子；平的
definition_en: an aircraft with wings and engines; a flat surface in geometry; a level of thought or existence; a carpenter's tool for smoothing wood; and flat or level
core_image: 跑道上银色的机翼，映出远处一块平整的水泥地
scene: 跑道尽头的灯一盏盏亮起，机翼在风里轻轻发抖。 The plane lifted off the runway just as the sun cleared the hills.
sceneCN: 这里 plane 是「飞机」（第 1 个义项：有翼有动力的航空器）；句意为太阳刚越过山脊，飞机就离开了跑道。图中可辨识物件：跑道灯、机翼、远处的山脊。

derivatives.zh: 由 plane 加形容词后缀 -ar 构成，义为「平面的」
由希腊语 aero-（空气）与 plane 复合而成，义为「飞机」（英式拼写）
由 plane 加表示工具或人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「刨床；刨工」

senses.title: An aircraft with wings and engines
senses.definition: a vehicle with wings and one or more engines that flies through the air
senses.definitionCN: 有翼、带一台或多台发动机、在空中飞行的交通工具
senses.example: Our plane was delayed by two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的飞机晚点了两个小时。
senses.why: This sense is a twentieth-century shortening of aeroplane, a French word built from Greek aer, air, and planer, to soar; the flat-surface word simply took over the spelling.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是二十世纪对 aeroplane 的缩略，那个法语词由希腊语 aer（空气）与 planer（翱翔）构成；它只是借用了表示「平面」那个词的拼写。

senses.title: A flat surface in geometry
senses.definition: a completely flat surface such that a straight line joining any two of its points lies wholly within it
senses.definitionCN: 完全平坦的面，面上任意两点连成的直线都整条落在该面内
senses.example: A plane has length and width but no thickness.
senses.exampleCN: 平面有长和宽，却没有厚度。
senses.why: Latin planum named level ground, and geometers took the same word for the perfectly even surface that ground only approximates.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 planum 指平地，几何学家借用同一个词，指地面只能近似达到的那种绝对平整的面。

senses.title: A level of thought or existence
senses.definition: a level on which ideas, activities or kinds of existence are considered to operate
senses.definitionCN: 思想、活动或存在方式被认为所处的某一层次
senses.example: Their argument moved onto a more practical plane.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的争论转到了一个更实际的层面上。
senses.why: Once a plane is an even surface, two things can sit on different surfaces without touching, so the word comes to name separate levels of experience.
senses.whyCN: 平面一旦成为一层平整的面，两样东西就能各处在不同的面上而互不接触，于是这个词也用来指经验中彼此分开的层次。

senses.title: A carpenter's tool for smoothing wood
senses.definition: a tool with a blade set in a block, pushed along wood to shave off thin layers and make it smooth
senses.definitionCN: 刀片装在木块里、沿木料推过以削去薄层使其平滑的工具
senses.example: He smoothed the edge of the board with a plane.
senses.exampleCN: 他用刨子把木板边缘刨平。
senses.why: The tool is named for the result it produces: a plane makes a surface flat, and the flat surface and the tool share one word in Latin and French.
senses.whyCN: 这件工具因它做出的结果得名：刨子把表面弄平，而「平面」与「工具」在拉丁语和法语里本来就共用一个词。

intro.en: Two different histories meet in one spelling: the flat surface and the woodworking tool come from Latin planus, while the aircraft is a shortened French coinage built on Greek aer.
intro.cn: 两种不同的来历汇成同一个拼写：平面与木工工具来自拉丁语 planus，而飞机则是对一个以希腊语 aer 造出的法语词的缩略。

items.en: Planus meant flat or level, and the noun planum named a flat surface or even ground.
items.cn: planus 意为平的、平坦的，名词 planum 指平面或平地。

items.en: Late Latin plana named a smoothing tool, and French plane kept that name for the carpenter's plane.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 plana 指一种弄平木料的工具，法语 plane 保留了这个名字，用来指木刨。

items.en: French aéroplane joined Greek aer, air, with planer, to soar or glide, and named a flying machine.
items.cn: 法语 aéroplane 把希腊语 aer（空气）与 planer（翱翔、滑翔）拼在一起，用来指飞行器。

items.en: English borrowed aeroplane and then clipped it to plane, so the aircraft inherited the spelling of the flat word.
items.cn: 英语借入 aeroplane，随后缩略为 plane，飞机就这样继承了那个表示「平」的词的拼写。

items.en: Modern English keeps all four senses, but plane is not related to plant or plantation, which go back to Latin planta, a sprout or a sole.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了四个义项；但 plane 与 plant、plantation 无关，后两者上溯到拉丁语 planta（嫩芽、脚掌）。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin flat family and two words that only share letters; the near-meaning group gathers aircraft and words for a flat level.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「平」这一族词，另收两个只是字母相像的词；近义组收航空器与表示平面层次的词。

entries.definition: Flat and open, or simple; it comes from the same Latin adjective for level ground.
entries.definitionCN: 平坦开阔的，或朴素的；来自同一个表示平地的拉丁形容词。

entries.definition: A scheme or a ground drawing; it shares the Latin root planus with the flat senses of plane.
entries.definitionCN: 方案或平面图；在「平面」这些义项上与本词共享拉丁词根 planus。

entries.definition: A body orbiting a star; Greek planan, to wander, lies behind it, so the likeness is spelling alone.
entries.definitionCN: 绕恒星运行的天体；背后是希腊语 planan（漫游），只是拼写相像。

entries.definition: A living thing that grows in soil; it comes from Latin planta, a sprout or a sole, not from planus, so the two are unrelated in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 在土里生长的生物；来自拉丁语 planta（嫩芽、脚掌），并非 planus，与此词词源不同。

entries.definition: Any vehicle that flies, including planes and helicopters.
entries.definitionCN: 任何能飞的交通工具，包括飞机与直升机。

entries.definition: A fast plane driven by jet engines.
entries.definitionCN: 由喷气发动机驱动的快速飞机。

entries.definition: A height or a standard, or a flat position.
entries.definitionCN: 高度、水准，或平坦的位置。

entries.definition: The outer or top layer of something.

normalIntro.en: The word carries two stories in one spelling: a Latin adjective for flat gave the surface and the tool, while a French word for soaring gave the aircraft.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词用同一个拼写装着两个故事：拉丁语表示「平」的形容词给出平面与工具，法语中表示翱翔的词则给出飞机。

normal.en: Latin planus means flat, so the geometric plane and the smoothing tool both start from an even surface.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 planus 意为平的，所以几何平面与刨平工具都从平整的面开始。

normal.en: The carpenter's plane is named for what it makes: a flat surface, the same idea as planum.
normal.cn: 木刨因它做出的结果得名：一个平整的面，和 planum 是同一个念头。

normal.en: The aircraft sense is a clipping of aeroplane, where aero- means air and planer means to soar.
normal.cn: 飞机这个义项是 aeroplane 的缩略，其中 aero- 意为空气，planer 意为翱翔。

normal.en: Plane is not related to plant: plant and plantation go back to Latin planta, a sprout or a sole of the foot.
normal.cn: plane 与 plant 无关：plant 与 plantation 上溯到拉丁语 planta，意为嫩芽或脚掌。

normal.en: Planar adds -ar and means lying in a plane, while planer adds -er and names the tool or the worker.
normal.cn: planar 加 -ar，意为位于一个平面内；planer 加 -er，指工具或刨工。

abstract.en: A word can wear one spelling while carrying two unrelated pasts, like two travellers sharing a coat.
abstract.cn: 一个词可以用同一个拼写背着两段互不相干的过去，就像两个旅人共用一件外套。

abstract.en: To smooth a board and to cross an ocean both aim at a surface that will not tilt.
abstract.cn: 刨平一块木板与飞越一片海洋，追求的都是一个不会倾斜的面。

abstract.en: A different plane of thought is simply a surface the other person is not standing on.
abstract.cn: 所谓另一个思维层面，不过是对方没有站在上面的那块面。

examples.en: Our plane was delayed by two hours.
examples.cn: 我们的飞机晚点了两个小时。

examples.en: A plane has length and width but no thickness.
examples.cn: 平面有长和宽，却没有厚度。

examples.en: He smoothed the edge of the board with a plane.
examples.cn: 他用刨子把木板边缘刨平。

root: plane 有两套来历：平面、刨子来自拉丁语 planus（平的）与 planum（平面）；飞机义则是 aeroplane 的缩略，来自希腊语 aer（空气）加法语 planer（翱翔）。plane 与 plant 不同源，plant 与 plantation 才同出拉丁语 planta（嫩芽、脚掌）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an even surface; the senses run from the geometric plane, to a level of thought, to the tool that makes wood even, and to the aircraft that took the spelling.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个平整的面；义项从几何平面，走到思维层面，再到把木头弄平的工具，最后是借用了这个拼写的飞机。

latinIntro.en: Latin forms are recorded for the flat and tool senses: the adjective planus, the noun planum, and the late noun plana for a smoothing tool.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「平面」与「工具」的义项有可考的拉丁形式：形容词 planus、名词 planum，以及晚期拉丁语中指弄平工具的名词 plana。

intro.en: Insect comes from Latin insectum, a cut-up thing, from in- (into) and secare (to cut). The name describes the notched waist that divides the body.
intro.cn: insect 来自拉丁语 insectum「被切分之物」，由 in-「切入」+ secare「切割」构成；名称刻画昆虫分节的腰身。

items.en: Latin secare meant to cut; it gave section, sector and scissors.
items.cn: 拉丁语 secare 意为切割；同根词有 section、sector、scissors。

items.en: in- plus secare formed insecare: to cut into, notched.
items.cn: in- 加 secare 构成 insecare：切入而留缺口。

items.en: Pliny used insectum as the calque of Greek entomon, the notched animal.
items.cn: 普林尼用 insectum 对译希腊语 entomon「有缺刻的动物」。

items.en: Greek entomon itself meant cut into segments.
items.cn: 希腊语 entomon 本义即「切成数节」。

items.en: English took insect from Latin in the scientific revival.
items.cn: 科学复兴时期英语从拉丁语借入 insect。

items.en: Modern English generalized it to all small bugs and added the figurative insult.
items.cn: 现代英语将其泛化为一切小虫，并添了轻蔑比喻。

dict_mnemonic.note: 搭配记忆 · 定冠词 the

sensesIntro.en: Same means alike, the very one, or unchanged over time.

branches.en: Identity means it is one thing, not two.

branches.en: No difference extends across time.

branches.en: The same person can stay unchanged for years.

intro.en: Same rarely takes prefixes but forms a few common compounds.

definition_zh: 责任；义务；职责；关税；值日
definition_en: something you must do because it is right or your job, or a tax on goods
core_image: 肩上稳稳放着一件必须扛住的东西
scene: 考试结束后，值日生独自留下擦净整块黑板。 It is the monitor's duty to lock the classroom after class.
sceneCN: 这里 duty 是「职责」（第 1 个义项：因身份或工作而必须做的事）；句意：下课后锁上教室是班长的职责。

derivatives.zh: duty 加 ful 构成，义为「尽职的；恭顺的」
dutiful 加 ly 构成，义为「尽职地」

senses.title: A required task
senses.definition: a task that your job or position requires you to do
senses.definitionCN: 因职务或身份而必须完成的任务
senses.example: It is the monitor's duty to lock the classroom.
senses.exampleCN: 锁上教室是班长的职责。
senses.why: The weight is fixed on the shoulder by your role, not by choice.
senses.whyCN: 这份重量由你的角色固定在肩上，而非个人选择。

senses.title: A moral obligation
senses.definition: something a person ought to do because it is right
senses.definitionCN: 因为正确而应当去做的事
senses.example: He helped the stranger out of a sense of duty.
senses.exampleCN: 他出于责任感帮助了那位陌生人。
senses.why: What the role demands inside a job, conscience demands inside a life.
senses.whyCN: 职务对工作的要求，变成了良心对人生的要求。

senses.title: A tax on goods
senses.definition: a payment required by a government on imported or exported goods
senses.definitionCN: 政府对进出口货物征收的款项
senses.example: We paid a small duty on the camera at the border.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在边境为这台相机缴纳了一笔小额关税。
senses.why: The payment is likewise owed because of a rule, not a choice.
senses.whyCN: 这笔钱同样因规则而必须缴纳，而非出于选择。

senses.title: Being on duty
senses.definition: a period when a person is working and responsible
senses.definitionCN: 某人负责工作的时间段
senses.example: The nurse is on duty until midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 这位护士值班到午夜。
senses.why: The task stretches into the hours when you carry it.
senses.whyCN: 任务延伸为承担它的时间段。

intro.en: Duty grew from the idea of what is owed, the same root that gives due.
intro.cn: duty 从「应缴、应欠之物」长出，与 due 同根。

items.en: Latin debere meant to owe, the ancestor of debt and due.
items.cn: 拉丁语 debere 意为欠债，是 debt 与 due 的祖先。

items.en: Old French deu meant owed or due, from the verb devoir.
items.cn: 古法语 deu 意为应欠的、应尽的，来自动词 devoir。

items.en: Middle English duete meant what one owes in conduct or payment.
items.cn: 中古英语 duete 指人在行为或钱款上应尽之物。

items.en: The word split into moral duty and customs duty on goods.
items.cn: 这个词分化为道德义务与货物关税两支。

items.en: Modern English added on duty and off duty for work shifts.
items.cn: 现代英语又添了 on duty 与 off duty 表示值班与否。

note.en: These words stand near duty in form or in meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 duty 相邻。

without import tax
something you must do by law or promise

normalIntro.en: Use the owed-thing picture and the duty family.
normalIntro.cn: 用「应尽之物」的画面和 duty 词族来记。

normal.en: duty and due share the idea of what is owed.
normal.cn: duty 与 due 共享「应尽之物」的意思。

normal.en: on duty and off duty flip the working switch.
normal.cn: on duty 与 off duty 切换工作的开关。

normal.en: import duty is the money owed at the border.
normal.cn: import duty 是边境上应缴的钱。

normal.en: a sense of duty is the inner voice that says you must.

normal.en: The plural drops y: duties.
normal.cn: 复数要把 y 变 i：duties。

abstract.en: Feel a steady weight settled on your shoulder that you cannot drop.
abstract.cn: 感受肩上一份放不下也卸不掉的稳稳重量。

abstract.en: See a stamp on a box at the border that says owed.
abstract.cn: 看见边境的箱子上盖着「应缴」的印章。

abstract.en: Hear the inner voice repeat the task until it is done.
abstract.cn: 听心里的声音反复催促，直到任务完成。

examples.en: Firefighters risk their lives in the line of duty.
examples.cn: 消防员在执行任务时冒着生命危险。

examples.en: Everyone paid duty on the goods they brought back.
examples.cn: 每个人为自己带回的货物缴纳了关税。

examples.en: She never refuses a duty that helps her classmates.
examples.cn: 她从不拒绝帮助同学的职责。

root: 来自拉丁语 debere（欠），经古法语 deu（应尽的）进入英语；本义为「应尽之物」，后分化出道德义务、关税与值班等义。

sensesIntro.en: Duty spreads from the required task to moral duty, customs duty and being on duty.
sensesIntro.cn: duty 从必须完成的任务出发，长出道德义务、关税与值班等义项。

branches.en: The task the role demands
branches.cn: 角色要求的任务

intro.en: Duty belongs to the owing family of due and dutiful.

definition_zh: 惊讶；意外；使惊讶
definition_en: an unexpected event or feeling, or to cause that feeling
core_image: 打开盒子的一瞬间，人们露出吃惊的表情
scene: 他的回答让大家十分惊讶。 His answer caused great surprise.
sceneCN: 这里 surprise 是「惊讶」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他的回答让大家十分惊讶。

derivatives.zh: 令人惊讶的
出乎意料地
感到惊讶的

senses.title: The feeling of shock
senses.definition: the feeling caused by something unexpected
senses.definitionCN: 由意外之事引起的感受
senses.example: His answer caused great surprise.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回答让大家十分惊讶。
senses.why: This is the core feeling sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的情绪义项。

senses.title: An unexpected event
senses.definition: something that happens without being expected
senses.definitionCN: 没有预料到而发生的事
senses.example: The party was a complete surprise.
senses.exampleCN: 这场聚会完全是个惊喜。
senses.why: Here the word names the event, not the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 这里指事件而非感受。

senses.title: To cause surprise
senses.definition: to make someone feel sudden wonder
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到突然的惊奇
senses.example: The news surprised everyone in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 这个消息让房间里所有人都感到惊讶。
senses.why: As a verb it names the act of causing the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 作动词时指引发这种感受。

intro.en: Surprise came from a French verb meaning to overtake suddenly.
intro.cn: surprise 来自一个意为「突然赶上」的法语动词。

items.en: Surprendre meant to overtake.

items.en: Surprise came to mean sudden wonder.

note.en: Surprise is compared with look-alike sur- words and with words for wonder.

sensesIntro.en: Surprise means the feeling of wonder, an unexpected event, or to cause that feeling.

core.en: Being caught by what we did not expect.

definition_zh: 天空；天气

scene: 傍晚的天空被夕阳染成了橘红色。 The evening sky turned orange in the sunset.

definition_zh: 通常；正常地；在正常情况下；一般说来
definition_en: usually or in most cases; in the ordinary or expected way; in a healthy physical state rather than an abnormal one
core_image: 一根竖杆稳稳立在底座上，左右两根绳拉得一样直
scene: 脚手架上的竖杆被重新校直，左右两根绳拉成一条线。 The pump was repaired and is now running normally.

pos.zh: 通常；正常地；在正常情况下

senses.title: In most cases; usually

senses.definitionCN: 以符合预期或能正确运作的方式，没有故障或例外
senses.example: The lift is working normally again.
senses.exampleCN: 电梯又恢复正常运行了。
senses.why: If something follows its own rule, it behaves as it should, so the same word moves from how often things happen to how they work.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西若照自己的规矩走，就是按应有的方式运作，于是同一个词从「事情多久发生一次」转到「事情怎么运作」。

senses.title: In a healthy physical state
senses.definition: in a normal physical or medical condition, not diseased or disordered
senses.definitionCN: 处于正常的身体或医学状态，没有病变或紊乱
senses.example: Her heart was beating normally after the rest.
senses.exampleCN: 休息之后她的心跳恢复了正常。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the word because health is defined by the body following its own rule, so a normal reading is one that matches the standard.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了这个词，因为健康本就以身体照自己的规矩运行为准，所以正常的读数就是与标准相符的那个。

senses.title: As one would expect if nothing interferes
senses.definition: used to say what should happen when no unusual event gets in the way
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明在没有意外事件妨碍时事情本应怎样
senses.example: Normally, the train would have arrived by now.
senses.exampleCN: 按说火车这会儿已经到了。
senses.why: The word can also open a sentence and set accidents aside, describing the course events take when nothing bends them away from the rule.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也能放在句首，把意外搁到一边，描述在没有外力使事物偏离规矩时它会走的那条路。

intro.en: Normally is the English adverb of normal, a Latin word for a carpenter's square that became the name of everything regular.
intro.cn: normally 是 normal 的英语副词；normal 这个拉丁词本指木匠的矩尺，后来成了「一切合规矩之物」的名称。

items.en: Norma meant a carpenter's square, the tool used to check a right angle, and it already carried the idea of a rule.
items.cn: norma 指木匠的矩尺，用来检查直角，本身已带有「规矩、标准」的意思。

items.en: Normalis meant made according to the square, hence regular and in proper order.
items.cn: normalis 意为按矩尺做成的，因此是「合乎规矩、秩序端正」的。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the seventeenth century, first for things built to a rule and later for what is usual.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个形容词，先指按规矩做成的东西，后来指通常的、普通的。

items.en: The adverb was formed by adding -ly, and it spread in the nineteenth century with the rise of statistics and standard measures.
items.cn: 这个副词由加 -ly 构成，随着统计学和标准计量的兴起在十九世纪流行开来。

items.en: Modern English uses it for what usually happens, for how a machine works and for a healthy bodily state.
items.cn: 现代英语用它指通常发生的事、机器运转的方式，以及健康的身体状态。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the adjective, its derived nouns and verbs, and the word for departure from the rule; the near-meaning group collects other adverbs of usual occurrence.
note.cn: 形近组收这个形容词、由它派生的名词与动词，以及表示偏离规矩的词；近义组收其他表示「通常发生」的副词。

entries.definition: Usual, regular, or in proper order.
entries.definitionCN: 通常的、有规律的，或秩序端正的。

entries.definition: The state of being usual or free from disorder.
entries.definitionCN: 处于通常状态或没有紊乱的状态。

entries.definition: To make something regular or standard.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物合乎常规或标准。

entries.definition: Departing from what is usual or expected.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离通常或预期情况的。

entries.definition: On most occasions, as a general rule.
entries.definitionCN: 在多数场合，作为一般规律。

entries.definition: In the ordinary course of things.
entries.definitionCN: 在事情通常的发展过程中。

entries.definition: Frequently, or by most people.
entries.definitionCN: 经常地，或由多数人来做地。

entries.definition: In the way that is characteristic of a kind.
entries.definitionCN: 以某一类事物典型的方式。

normalIntro.en: The word carries a carpenter's square into everyday life, turning a tool for checking right angles into an adverb for what usually happens.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把木匠的矩尺带进日常生活，把检查直角的工具变成了表示「通常如何」的副词。

normal.en: Latin norma was a carpenter's square, so normal first meant cut to a right angle.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 norma 是木匠的矩尺，所以 normal 最初指按直角裁成。

normal.en: The suffix -ly turns the adjective normal into an adverb without changing its meaning.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ly 把形容词 normal 变成副词，含义不变。

normal.en: Normally usually sits before the verb, as in it normally works.
normal.cn: normally 常放在动词前，如 it normally works。

normal.en: In statistics a normally distributed quantity follows the bell curve, a direct heir of the word's sense of a standard.
normal.cn: 统计学里正态分布的量顺着钟形曲线，正是这个词「标准」义的直系后代。

normal.en: Abnormal adds a prefix of departure, so the pair marks the line between the rule and the exception.
normal.cn: abnormal 加了一个表示「离开」的前缀，这一对词就标出规矩与例外之间的界线。

abstract.en: A word taken from a tool for measuring right angles now measures ordinary life, which shows how deeply English borrows the workshop for the mind.
abstract.cn: 一个取自量直角工具的借词如今用来衡量日常生活，可见英语向工坊借词借得有多深。

abstract.en: Normally is a quiet promise about the future: it describes the path things take unless something bends them aside.
abstract.cn: normally 是对未来的一句轻声保证：它描述在没有外力把事物掰弯时它们会走的路。

abstract.en: The same adverb covers habit, machinery and health because all three are judged against a rule the thing is expected to follow.
abstract.cn: 同一个副词能覆盖习惯、机器和健康，因为三者都是拿「事物本应遵守的规矩」来评判的。

examples.en: Normally, the shop closes at six.
examples.cn: 通常这家店六点关门。

examples.en: The lift is working normally again.
examples.cn: 电梯又恢复正常运行了。

examples.en: Her heart was beating normally after the rest.
examples.cn: 休息之后她的心跳恢复了正常。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺曼底」——诺曼底的日子按老规矩来，一切都正常；记住 normally 是正常地。

root: normal 源自拉丁语 normalis（按矩尺做成的、合乎规矩的），更早出自 norma（木匠的矩尺）；加上英语副词词尾 -ly 构成 normally。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is following a rule; it divides into usual frequency, correct working order, healthy condition and the expected course of events.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是照着规矩走；由此分出通常的频率、正确的运作方式、健康的状态，以及事情本应走的路线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a upright post reset on its base, two ropes pulled into one straight line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根竖杆在底座上重新校直，两条绳被拉成一条直线。

branches.en: a shop shutter coming down at the same hour each day
branches.cn: 每天同一时刻落下的店门

branches.en: a train expected at the platform by the timetable
branches.cn: 按时刻表该到站的火车

branches.en: a lift rising smoothly after a repair
branches.cn: 修好后平稳上升的电梯

branches.en: a pulse steady after a long rest
branches.cn: 久歇之后平稳的脉搏

branches.en: a machine and a body both back on their rule
branches.cn: 机器与身体都回到各自的规矩上

intro.en: The word rests on the Latin names for a carpenter's square and for what is made to its measure, with English suffixes around the base.
intro.cn: 这个词立在拉丁语中「矩尺」与「按尺做成之物」的名称上，基础词周围还有英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin norma and its adjective normalis supply the base of the word, and the adverb ending is English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 norma 及其形容词 normalis 提供这个词的底子，副词词尾则是英语的。

items.meaningCN: 按矩尺做成的；合乎规矩的

latinEntries.meaningCN: 按矩尺做成的；合乎规矩的

definition_zh: 害怕；恐惧；担忧；敬畏；害怕做某事
definition_en: an unpleasant feeling caused by the belief that something dangerous or painful might happen, or the act of being afraid
core_image: 黑暗里一步不敢挪动的身体，心跳加速，眼睛盯着可能出现的危险
scene: 停电的楼道里脚步声由远及近，孩子紧紧抓住门框。 She could not move for fear of waking the dog.
sceneCN: 这里 fear 是名词，指「恐惧」这一情绪，对应第 1 个义项；句意为她一动不动，生怕惊醒狗。

derivatives.zh: 可怕的；害怕的（fear 加形容词后缀 -ful，指充满恐惧或令人恐惧）
无畏的；不怕的（fear 加 -less，指没有恐惧）
害怕地；非常地（fearful 加副词后缀 -ly）
无畏地（fearless 加副词后缀 -ly）

senses.title: The feeling of being afraid
senses.definition: an unpleasant emotion caused by the belief that someone or something is dangerous
senses.definitionCN: 因相信某人某物有危险而产生的不快情绪
senses.example: He has a fear of spiders.
senses.exampleCN: 他害怕蜘蛛。
senses.why: The body reacts before thinking, so the word first names the raw feeling itself.
senses.whyCN: 身体先于思考起反应，所以这个词首先指那种原始情绪。

senses.title: A worry about something specific
senses.definition: a worry that something bad may happen
senses.definitionCN: 对坏事可能发生的担忧
senses.example: Her biggest fear is failing the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 她最大的顾虑是考试不及格。
senses.why: When the danger is distant and imagined, the feeling softens into a worry.
senses.whyCN: 当危险遥远而只是想象时，这种感觉便弱化为担忧。

senses.title: To be afraid of something
senses.definition: to feel afraid of a person, thing or situation
senses.definitionCN: 对某人、某物或某种情况感到害怕
senses.example: Do not fear the dark; fear what hides in it.
senses.exampleCN: 不要怕黑，要怕藏在黑暗里的东西。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb: the feeling itself becomes the act of feeling it.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：情绪本身变成「感到这种情绪」这一动作。

senses.title: To expect something bad
senses.definition: to think that something bad has happened or will happen
senses.definitionCN: 认为坏事已经或将要发生
senses.example: I fear we are too late.
senses.exampleCN: 恐怕我们已经太迟了。
senses.why: Expecting the worst is fear pointed at the future, so the verb shifts to prediction.
senses.whyCN: 预期最坏的事就是指向未来的恐惧，于是动词偏向「料想」。

senses.title: Respect mixed with awe
senses.definition: respect for someone powerful, mixed with dread
senses.definitionCN: 对强者的敬重，其中夹杂畏惧
senses.example: They feared the old master's judgment.
senses.exampleCN: 他们敬畏老匠人的评判。
senses.why: Power that can hurt you earns both respect and dread, so fear stretches to cover awe.
senses.whyCN: 能伤害你的力量同时赢得敬重与畏惧，于是 fear 扩展到「敬畏」。

intro.en: Fear is a native Germanic word, grown from an Old English noun for sudden danger, and it has carried both emotion and expectation for a thousand years.
intro.cn: fear 是日耳曼本族词，由古英语表「突然危险」的名词发展而来，千年来一直兼指情绪与预料。

items.en: A reconstructed Germanic root feraz meant 'danger' or 'that which attacks'; cousins appear in German Gefahr.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构的日耳曼词根 feraz 意为「危险」或「来袭之物」；德语 Gefahr 是同族词。

items.en: Old English fer meant 'sudden danger or calamity', and the verb form grew beside it.
items.cn: 古英语 fer 意为「突发的危险或灾祸」，动词形式也随之生长。

items.en: Middle English fere covered both the emotion and the expected harm, as in for fear of.
items.cn: 中古英语 fere 兼指情绪与预期的祸害，如 for fear of（以免）。

items.en: Spelling settled as fear, and the word now leads a large family: fearful, fearless, fearfully.
items.cn: 现代英语拼写定为 fear，并形成大家族：fearful、fearless、fearfully。

items.en: Psychology and daily speech keep fear as the baseline word for all anxiety-like feelings.
items.cn: 心理学与日常语言都把 fear 当作一切类焦虑情绪的基础词。

note.en: Look-alikes share the shape fea-; near-meaning words occupy the wider field of dread and worry.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fea- 字形；近义组占据恐惧与担忧这一更大的义场。

entries.definition: to receive sound with the ears; one letter apart and unrelated in origin
entries.definitionCN: 用耳朵接收声音；只差一个字母，词源无关

entries.definition: the organ of hearing; fear without the f
entries.definitionCN: 听觉器官；即 fear 去掉 f

entries.definition: money paid for a journey; close in sound but a different root
entries.definitionCN: 车费；发音相近但词源不同

entries.definition: great fear of something that may happen
entries.definitionCN: 对将临之事的强烈恐惧

entries.definition: extreme and overwhelming fear
a state of nervous worry about the future
entries.definitionCN: 对未来的紧张忧虑；焦虑

normalIntro.en: Five handles from the family and the everyday phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自词族与日常短语的记忆抓手。

normal.en: fear has three letters f-e-a-r, like four quick heartbeats when danger appears.
normal.cn: fear 四个字母，像危险出现时的四次快速心跳。

normal.en: fearful means full of fear, fearless means without it: same root, opposite endings.
normal.cn: fearful 是充满恐惧，fearless 是毫无恐惧：同根而词尾相反。

normal.en: for fear of doing something means you avoid it to stay safe.
normal.cn: for fear of doing something 表示为安全起见而避免做某事。

normal.en: I fear so / I fear not is a polite way to say yes or no about bad news.
normal.cn: I fear so / I fear not 是对坏消息礼貌地说「恐怕是/恐怕不是」。

normal.en: German Gefahr means danger, a cousin from the same old root.
normal.cn: 德语 Gefahr 意为「危险」，是同一古老词根的亲戚。

abstract.en: Fear is a smoke alarm wired to your imagination, loud even when the fire is far away.
abstract.cn: 恐惧像接到想象上的烟雾报警器，火还很远就已经大响。

abstract.en: Dread is fear with a calendar: it counts the days to something bad.
abstract.cn: dread 是带日历的恐惧：它替你倒数坏日子的到来。

abstract.en: Awe is fear wearing a crown: the same alarm, pointed at greatness.
abstract.cn: 敬畏是戴王冠的恐惧：同一台警报，对准的是伟大。

examples.en: He overcame his fear of public speaking by practising weekly.
examples.cn: 他通过每周练习克服了当众讲话的恐惧。

examples.en: I fear that the train has already left.
examples.cn: 恐怕火车已经开走了。

examples.en: The villagers lived in fear of the flood every summer.
examples.cn: 村民每年夏天都生活在对洪水的恐惧中。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「菲尔怕」—— 菲尔一听到怪声就害怕 → fear 恐惧、害怕

root: 出自古英语 fer「突发的危险」，可上溯至重构的日耳曼词根（一般认为与表「危险、来袭」的语族相关）；词义由「危险」转为「对危险的感受」。

sensesIntro.en: From the raw feeling outward to specific worries, the verb of feeling, prediction of bad news, and awe.
sensesIntro.cn: 从原始情绪出发，扩展到具体顾虑、动词用法、对坏消息的料想以及敬畏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body frozen in the dark, eyes fixed on a possible danger.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑暗中僵住的身体，眼睛盯着可能的危险。

branches.en: THE FEELING: fear itself as emotion.
branches.cn: 情绪：恐惧这种感受本身。

branches.en: THE WORRY: a specific imagined bad event.
branches.cn: 顾虑：具体的、想象中的坏事。

branches.en: THE ACTION: being afraid as a verb.
branches.cn: 动作：作为动词的害怕。

branches.en: THE PREDICTION: expecting the worst.
branches.cn: 预料：预期坏事发生。

branches.en: THE RESPECT: awe before power.
branches.cn: 敬畏：面对强者的敬重。

intro.en: Fear builds a compact family with two opposite adjectives and their adverbs.
intro.cn: fear 构成一个紧凑的词族：两个意义相反的形容词及其副词。

latinIntro.en: Fear has no Latin relatives; the family is purely Germanic, built with native suffixes.
latinIntro.cn: fear 没有拉丁同族词；词族纯出日耳曼本族，用本族后缀构成。

items.meaning: filled with fear or causing fear
items.example: A fearful crash woke the street.
items.exampleCN: 可怕的撞击声惊醒整条街。

items.example: The fearless reporter followed the story.
He whispered for fear of being heard.
items.exampleCN: 他压低声音以免被人听见。

items.example: Her fear of heights kept her inside.

definition_zh: 和平的；宁静的；平和的
definition_en: without war or fighting; quiet and calm; or gentle in temperament and not eager to argue
core_image: 午后的院子没有风，一只猫在阳光下慢慢闭上眼睛
scene: 乡下的小院只听得见虫鸣，竹椅上的人把书合上，任由阳光落在膝头。 It was a peaceful afternoon, and nobody wanted to break the silence.
sceneCN: 这里是「宁静的」（第 2 个义项：环境安静、不被打扰）；句意是那是一个宁静的下午，谁也不愿打破这份安静。画面里有小院、虫鸣、竹椅与合上的书。

derivatives.zh: 由 peaceful 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，义为「平和地；安静地」
由 peaceful 加名词词尾 -ness 构成，义为「宁静；平和」
由 peaceful 加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「不平静的；不安宁的」

senses.title: Free from war or violence
senses.definition: describing a place, time or solution in which there is no war or fighting
senses.definitionCN: 形容没有战争或暴力的地方、时期或解决办法
senses.example: They hoped for a peaceful settlement of the dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 他们希望这场争端能得到和平解决。
senses.why: Peace plus -ful means full of peace, and the first and most public kind of peace is the absence of war.
senses.whyCN: peace 加 -ful 意为「充满和平」，而最公开、最基本的一种和平就是没有战争。

senses.title: Quiet and undisturbed
senses.definition: quiet and calm, with nothing loud, hurried or troubling going on
senses.definitionCN: 安静平和，没有喧闹、匆忙或令人烦扰的事情发生
senses.example: The village was peaceful at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明时分的村子十分宁静。
senses.why: If a country can be full of peace, so can a room; the same adjective simply shifts from public order to the feel of a place.
senses.whyCN: 既然一个国家可以「充满和平」，一间屋子也可以；同一个形容词只是从公共秩序转到地方的氛围上。

senses.title: Gentle and not inclined to argue
senses.definition: having a calm temper and avoiding quarrels or violence
senses.definitionCN: 性情温和，避免争吵或使用暴力
senses.example: He is a peaceful man who avoids quarrels.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个平和的人，遇事总避开争吵。
senses.why: Push the adjective inside a person and it describes someone who carries the same absence of conflict in their temper.
senses.whyCN: 把这个形容词推进一个人心里，它描述的就是把同一种「不起冲突」带进性情的人。

intro.en: Peaceful is a plain English compound: a Latin noun for agreement, filtered through French, plus the old suffix that means full of.
intro.cn: peaceful 是一个朴素的英语复合词：经法语过滤的拉丁语「约定」名词，加上表示「充满」的古老词尾。

items.en: Pax named an agreement and the state that followed it, and its stem pac- feeds the whole family of peace words.
items.cn: pax 指约定以及约定之后的状态，其词干 pac- 支撑起整个和平词族。

items.en: Old French pais brought the noun to England with the sense of peace and quiet.
items.cn: 古法语 pais 把这个名词带进英格兰，义为和平与安宁。

items.en: Middle English pees named both public peace and personal calm, and it could already take the adjective ending.
items.cn: 中古英语 pees 兼具公共和平与个人平静两义，并且已经可以接形容词词尾。

items.en: The suffix -full meant full of or marked by, and it survives in modern English as the shorter -ful.
items.cn: 词尾 -full 意为「充满……的」，在现代英语中简化为更短的 -ful。

items.en: Modern English joined the two parts and spread the adjective from politics to places and to people.
items.cn: 现代英语把两部分合成 peaceful，并把这个形容词从政治扩展到地方与人的性情。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the noun and the other words built on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group collects adjectives for quiet and untroubled conditions.
note.cn: 形近组收那个名词以及建立在同一拉丁词干上的其他词；近义组收形容安静无忧状态的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun meaning freedom from war or a state of calm.
entries.definitionCN: 表示没有战争或心境安宁的名词。

entries.definition: In a quiet and calm way, without fighting.
entries.definitionCN: 以安静平和的方式，没有争斗。

entries.definition: Willing to avoid argument; fond of peace.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意避免争执的；爱好和平的。

entries.definition: To calm an angry person, or to end violence.
entries.definitionCN: 使愤怒的人平静，或终止暴力。

entries.definition: Not excited, worried or disturbed.
entries.definitionCN: 不激动、不担忧、不被打扰的。

entries.definition: Quiet and peaceful, often used of places and water.
entries.definitionCN: 安静平和的，常用于地方与水面。

entries.definition: Calm and untroubled, with a feeling of deep quiet.
entries.definitionCN: 平静无忧、带有深沉宁静感的。

entries.definition: Making little or no noise.

normalIntro.en: The adjective is the noun plus a suffix, so every sense can be read as a kind of fullness of peace.
normalIntro.cn: 这个形容词就是名词加一个词尾，因此每个义项都可以读成某种「满是和平」的状态。

normal.en: Peaceful is peace plus -ful, so it literally means full of peace.
normal.cn: peaceful 就是 peace 加 -ful，字面意思就是「充满和平」。

normal.en: The suffix keeps a single l, unlike the separate word full.
normal.cn: 这个词尾只写一个 l，与单独成词的 full 不同。

normal.en: A peaceful place is one where nothing disturbs you, which is the calm sense of the noun pushed outward.
normal.cn: 宁静的地方就是没有什么来打扰你的地方，这是名词「平静」义向外推的结果。

normal.en: A peaceful person is not weak; the word describes someone who chooses not to quarrel.
normal.cn: 平和的人并不软弱；这个词描述的是选择不争吵的人。

normal.en: The comparative takes more and most because the adjective is too long for -er and -est.
normal.cn: 比较级用 more、最高级用 most，因为这个词太长，不能加 -er 与 -est。

abstract.en: Peaceful describes a condition rather than an act: it says what is missing, namely noise and conflict.
abstract.cn: peaceful 描述的是状态而不是动作：它说的是缺少了什么，即噪声与冲突。

abstract.en: The same adjective can qualify a village, an afternoon and a man, because calmness looks alike in all three.
abstract.cn: 同一个形容词能修饰村庄、下午和人，因为安静在三者身上看起来很像。

abstract.en: A word made by adding full to peace suggests that peace is a substance one can be filled with.
abstract.cn: 把 full 加到 peace 上构成的词，暗示和平是一种可以被充满的东西。

examples.en: The two states reached a peaceful agreement.
examples.cn: 这两个国家达成了和平协议。

examples.en: It was a peaceful evening with no traffic and no voices.
examples.cn: 那是一个没有车声、没有人语的宁静夜晚。

examples.en: She has a peaceful way of settling arguments.
examples.cn: 她有一种平和的化解争执的方式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮斯佛」——满心都是 peace，人就平和了；peaceful 是平和的。

root: 由名词 peace（和平）加形容词词尾 -ful（充满……的）构成；peace 来自拉丁语 pax，属格 pacis，经古法语 pais 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a place or person filled with peace; the senses divide into the public absence of war, the quiet of a place, and the gentleness of a temper.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是充满和平的地方或人；义项分出公共层面的没有战争、地方的安静，以及性情的温和。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a courtyard without wind, where a cat slowly closes its eyes in the sun.
core.cn: 核心意象：没有风的午后小院，一只猫在阳光下慢慢闭上眼睛。

branches.en: two delegations signing a settlement instead of fighting
branches.cn: 两个代表团以签署协议代替开战

branches.en: a courtyard where only insects can be heard
branches.cn: 只听得见虫鸣的小院

branches.en: a man who lowers his voice when others begin to shout
branches.cn: 别人开始喊时反而放低声音的人

branches.en: a public truce and a private temper sharing one word
branches.cn: 公共的停火与私人的性情共用一个词

branches.en: a quiet afternoon and a quiet man
branches.cn: 安静的下午与安静的人

intro.en: The word is the noun peace with the old suffix -ful, so its parts are a Latin root of agreement and an English marker of fullness.
intro.cn: 这个词是名词 peace 加古老词尾 -ful，因此它的成分是一个表示约定的拉丁词根，和一个标示「充满」的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 使丧失能力；使伤残；（技术）使失效；使停用
definition_en: to make someone unable to do something, or to stop a machine working
core_image: 一只手按下开关，机器停止转动
scene: 机房设备维护课上，老师演示操作。 Remember to disable the alarm before you open the door.
sceneCN: 这里 disable 是「使失效、停用」（第 2 个义项：让设备停止工作）；句意是开门前记得先解除警报。

derivatives.zh: disable 的词基，义为「能力」
过去分词作形容词，义为「残疾的；失效的」
反构词，义为「使能够」
disable 加名词后缀构成，义为「残疾；功能障碍」

senses.title: To make someone unable
senses.definition: to hurt someone so that part of their body or mind cannot work normally
senses.definitionCN: 使身体或心智的一部分无法正常工作
senses.example: The illness disabled his left leg for months.
senses.exampleCN: 那场病让他的左腿几个月不能活动。
senses.why: Able means can do; the prefix dis- takes the power away, so disable is to un-able someone.
senses.whyCN: able 表示「能够」，前缀 dis- 把能力拿走，disable 即「使失去能力」。

senses.title: To stop a machine or system
senses.definition: to switch off or break a device so it cannot work
senses.definitionCN: 关掉或破坏设备使其无法运转
senses.example: The virus disabled the whole computer system.
senses.exampleCN: 病毒使整个计算机系统瘫痪了。
senses.why: A machine is able to work; disabling it is removing that ability too.
senses.whyCN: 机器有运转的能力，disable 同样是把这个能力移除。

intro.en: Disable is the prefix dis- on the old verb abide.
intro.cn: disable 是前缀 dis- 加在古动词 abide 上构成的。

items.en: Old French abler meant to make able, from Latin habilis (easy to handle).
items.cn: 古法语 abler 意为使能够，出自拉丁语 habilis（易于掌握的）。

items.en: English formed ablen, to make able.
items.cn: 中古英语构成 ablen，意为使能够。

items.en: Adding dis- (apart, away) built disable in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 十五世纪加上 dis-（离开、除去）构成 disable。

items.en: First it meant to weaken legally or physically.
items.cn: 最初指在法律或身体上削弱。

items.en: Modern use covers injuries, and switching off machines and programmes.
items.cn: 现代用法涵盖身体伤残以及关闭机器与程序。

note.en: These words share the able root or the dis- prefix.
note.cn: 这些词同出 able 词根，或带 dis- 前缀。

noun: the state of being unable

power to do
not able
to make weaker
to badly hurt a body
