normalIntro.en: Split the word: dis- (away) + able (can do).
normalIntro.cn: 拆开单词：dis-（除去）+ able（能够）。

normal.en: disable = dis + able, take the ability away.
normal.cn: disable = dis + able，把能力拿走。

normal.en: enable is the opposite: give the ability.
normal.cn: enable 是反义词：赋予能力。

normal.en: the disabled means disabled people as a group.
normal.cn: the disabled 指残疾人群体。

normal.en: disable the alarm means switch it off.
normal.cn: disable the alarm 意思是关掉警报。

normal.en: remember abil- hides inside: ability, disable, enable.
normal.cn: 注意 abil- 藏在 ability、disable、enable 里面。

abstract.en: Picture a power plug pulled out of the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象电源插头被从墙上拔下。

abstract.en: Feel a hand press the big red stop button.
abstract.cn: 体会手按下红色大停止键的感觉。

abstract.en: See a robot freeze in the middle of a step.
abstract.cn: 想象机器人走到一半突然定格。

examples.en: The security guard disabled the alarm before checking the hall.
examples.cn: 保安在检查大厅前先解除了警报。

examples.en: A heavy rain disabled the traffic lights on our street.
examples.cn: 一场大雨使我们街上的红绿灯失灵了。

examples.en: Grandpa's eyes were disabled by the illness, so we read news for him.
examples.cn: 爷爷的眼睛因病失明，我们便读新闻给他听。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弟斯诶波」——弟弟撕掉了电池（battery），机器立刻失去能力

root: 来自中古英语 disable，dis-（除去）+ ablen（使能够）；ablen 出自古法语 abler，源于拉丁语 habilis（易于掌握的）。

sensesIntro.en: Disable removes ability from a body or a machine.
sensesIntro.cn: disable 表示把能力从人或机器身上移除。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pulling out the power plug
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手拔掉电源插头

branches.en: A body that cannot work normally
branches.cn: 无法正常运作的身体

branches.en: A machine that stops
branches.cn: 停止运转的机器

branches.en: One verb, two kinds of ability
branches.cn: 一个动词，两种「能力」

branches.en: Alarms, systems and functions switched off
branches.cn: 被关闭的警报、系统与功能

branches.en: Help and care after injury
branches.cn: 伤残之后的帮助与照顾

intro.en: Disable wears its meaning on the outside: dis- + able.
intro.cn: disable 的意思写在字面上：dis- + able。

latinIntro.en: The able root goes back to Latin habilis, easy to handle.
latinIntro.cn: able 词根可追溯到拉丁语 habilis（易于掌握的）。

definition_zh: 胡椒；胡椒粉；辣椒；撒胡椒粉
definition_en: a hot spice made from dried berries, the hollow fruit of related plants used as a vegetable, or to scatter this spice over food
core_image: 手指捻动小瓶，深色粉末簌簌落在食物上
scene: 灶台前，厨师把刚煎好的牛排放在案板上，手腕一抖，细粉落满表面。 The chef peppered the steak and slid it onto the plate.
sceneCN: 这里是「撒胡椒粉」（第 3 个义项：动词用法）；句意为厨师给牛排撒上胡椒，再把它滑进盘子。

derivatives.zh: 由 pepper 加后缀 -y 构成，义为「胡椒味的；辛辣的；脾气急的」
由 pepper 与 corn 复合而成，义为「胡椒粒」
由 pepper 与 mint 复合而成，指薄荷，因味道刺激而得名
由 pepper 与 mill 复合而成，义为「胡椒研磨器」

senses.title: The spice made from dried berries
senses.definition: a hot spice made from the dried berries of a tropical vine, used as a powder or in whole grains
senses.definitionCN: 由热带藤本植物的干果制成的辛辣香料，可磨成粉或整粒使用
senses.example: Season the soup with salt and freshly ground pepper.
senses.exampleCN: 用盐和现磨的胡椒给汤调味。
senses.why: Latin piper named the spice itself, and English kept it as a mass noun for the powder that is shaken over food.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 piper 指的就是这种香料本身，英语把它保留为不可数名词，指撒在食物上的粉末。

senses.title: The hollow fruit eaten as a vegetable
senses.definition: the hollow fruit of plants in the same family, eaten as a vegetable in colours such as green, red and yellow
senses.definitionCN: 同科植物的中空果实，作为蔬菜食用，有绿、红、黄等颜色
senses.example: She stuffed the peppers with rice and baked them.
senses.exampleCN: 她把米饭塞进辣椒里烤熟。
senses.why: The spice and the vegetable come from the same plant family, so one name covers both, and cooks count the vegetable one by one.
senses.whyCN: 香料和蔬菜来自同一科植物，于是一个名称覆盖两者；而做菜时蔬菜是一颗颗数的。

senses.title: To scatter pepper over food
senses.definition: to shake pepper or a similar powder over food before eating or cooking
senses.definitionCN: 在烹调或进食前把胡椒或类似粉末撒在食物上
senses.example: He peppered the eggs and handed me the plate.
senses.exampleCN: 他给鸡蛋撒上胡椒，把盘子递给我。
senses.why: The verb is the noun set in motion: the powder leaves the shaker in small specks and lands on whatever lies below.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是让名词动起来：粉末从瓶里成小点落下，落在下面的东西上。

senses.title: To cover with many small things
senses.definition: to cover a surface with many small marks or objects, or to hit someone with a rapid stream of questions, shots or criticism
senses.definitionCN: 用许多小点或小物布满一个表面，或向某人连续发出问题、射击或批评
senses.example: Reporters peppered her with questions as she left the court.
senses.exampleCN: 她离开法庭时，记者们连珠炮般向她提问。
senses.why: Once pepper is a shower of specks, the verb can describe anything arriving that way, so words and bullets behave like grains of powder.
senses.whyCN: 一旦胡椒被看成一阵密集的小点，这个动词就能描写任何以这种方式到来的东西，于是话语和子弹都像粉末颗粒。

intro.en: Pepper travelled west along trade routes, from an Indic name for long pepper through Greek and Latin into Old English.
intro.cn: pepper 沿着贸易路线西行，从印度方面表示长胡椒的名称，经希腊语、拉丁语进入古英语。

items.en: Sanskrit pippali named long pepper, and the deeper origin of the word is generally thought to lie outside Indo-European, possibly in a Dravidian language.
items.cn: 梵语 pippali 指长胡椒，这个词更早的来源一般认为在印欧语之外，可能来自某种达罗毗荼语。

items.en: Greek took the word as peperi, and Greek traders carried both the spice and the name westward.
items.cn: 希腊语把它写作 peperi，希腊商人把香料和名称一起带向西方。

items.en: Latin piper named the spice, and Roman cooks used it so heavily that it became a common item of trade.
items.cn: 拉丁语 piper 指胡椒，罗马厨师用得极多，使它成了常见的贸易货品。

items.en: Old English borrowed the Latin word as pipor, and the spelling later shifted to pepper.
items.cn: 古英语借入拉丁词写作 pipor，后来拼写演变为 pepper。

items.en: Modern English keeps the spice and the vegetable under one word and uses the verb for any dense shower of things.
items.cn: 现代英语用同一个词表示香料和蔬菜，并用动词描写任何密集袭来的一阵东西。

note.en: The look-alike group collects derived words and compounds built on the spice name; the near-meaning group collects other seasonings and members of the pepper family.
note.cn: 形近组收由这一香料名构成的派生词与复合词；近义组收其他调味料以及胡椒家族的成员。

entries.definition: Tasting of pepper, or quick to anger.
A single dried berry of the pepper plant.
A small device for grinding peppercorns.
A mint plant with a strong cool taste.
entries.definitionCN: 一种薄荷，名字取自胡椒般的刺激味道，与胡椒并非同一种植物。

entries.definition: A small hot pepper used in cooking.
entries.definitionCN: 做菜用的小而辣的辣椒。

entries.definition: A dried plant substance used to flavour food.
entries.definitionCN: 用于给食物调味的干燥植物性香料。

entries.definition: The botanical name for peppers and their fruit.
entries.definitionCN: 辣椒属及其果实的植物学名称。

entries.definition: Salt, pepper or spices added to improve flavour.
entries.definitionCN: 为提味而加的盐、胡椒或香料。

normalIntro.en: The word keeps a Latin spice name on top of an older Indic root, and its family stays close to the kitchen and to the idea of many small specks.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词在更古老的印度词根之上保存了一个拉丁香料名，同族词始终贴近厨房，也贴近「许多小颗粒」这个意象。

normal.en: Piper is the Latin name, and the English word keeps the double p of the original.
normal.cn: piper 是拉丁名，英语词保留了原词的双写 p。

normal.en: The spice is uncountable, so you say some pepper, while the vegetable is countable, so you say two peppers.
normal.cn: 香料不可数，说 some pepper；蔬菜可数，说 two peppers。

normal.en: Peppery adds -y, the suffix that turns a noun into a quality, so the word means full of pepper.
normal.cn: peppery 加 -y，这个后缀把名词变成性质，所以词义是「充满胡椒的」。

normal.en: A peppercorn is one grain, which is why a mill grinds corns rather than powder.
normal.cn: peppercorn 是一粒，所以研磨器磨的是颗粒而不是粉末。

normal.en: Pepper with questions borrows the picture of many small grains hitting a surface at once.
normal.cn: pepper with questions 借用了许多小颗粒同时打在一个表面上的画面。

abstract.en: A spice and a vegetable share one name because both come from the same family, and language often prefers the family resemblance over precision.
abstract.cn: 香料和蔬菜共用一个名字，因为两者同科；语言常常更看重亲缘相似，而不是精确区分。

abstract.en: To pepper someone with questions is to treat words as if they were grains thrown by the handful.
abstract.cn: 用问题 pepper 某人，就是把话语当成一把把撒出去的颗粒。

abstract.en: The word travelled from a Sanskrit name for long pepper to a Latin trade good to an English kitchen, carried by the same appetite.
abstract.cn: 这个词从梵语的长胡椒之名，走到拉丁语的贸易货，再走到英语的厨房，靠的是同一种胃口。

examples.en: Season the soup with salt and freshly ground pepper.
examples.cn: 用盐和现磨的胡椒给汤调味。

examples.en: The garden is full of green and red peppers.
examples.cn: 园子里长满了青椒和红椒。

examples.en: Journalists peppered her with questions as she left the court.
examples.cn: 她离开法庭时，记者们连珠炮般向她提问。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拍拍」——往牛排上拍拍胡椒瓶，粉末落下来；记住 pepper 是胡椒。

root: 古英语 pipor 借自拉丁语 piper，更早可追到希腊语 peperi 与梵语 pippali（长胡椒）；同族词多与这种香料有关。

sensesIntro.en: The word names the spice, the vegetable from the same family, the act of scattering it, and any dense shower of small things.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词指香料、同科的蔬菜、撒粉的动作，以及任何密集落下的小东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand shaking a small jar so that dark powder falls onto food.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指捻动小瓶，深色粉末簌簌落在食物上。

branches.en: a mill grinding dried berries into powder
branches.cn: 研磨器把干果磨成粉

branches.en: a hollow red fruit stuffed with rice
branches.cn: 塞满米饭的中空红果

branches.en: a hand shaking powder over a steak
branches.cn: 手把粉末撒在牛排上

branches.en: questions arriving like thrown grains
branches.cn: 问题像撒出的颗粒一样袭来

branches.en: from scattering powder to scattering words
branches.cn: 从撒粉末到撒话语

intro.en: The word is a Latin spice name carried into English, and its family grows through English compounds and suffixes around the kitchen.
intro.cn: 这个词是传入英语的拉丁香料名，同族词围绕厨房，靠英语的复合与后缀生长。

latinIntro.en: The Latin word piper is the direct source of the English name, and it came to Latin from Greek, which took it from an Indic word for long pepper.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 piper 是英语名称的直接来源；它由希腊语传入拉丁语，而希腊语又借自印度方面表示长胡椒的词。

items.meaning: full of pepper, sharp in taste

definition_zh: 旅程；行程；历程
definition_en: an act of travelling from one place to another, especially a long one, or a long process of change
core_image: 一条从地平线开头、一直延伸到看不见尽头的路
scene: 清早的车站，人提着行李站在站台尽头，列车的灯从远处亮起来。 The journey takes nine hours if the trains run on time.
sceneCN: 这里 journey 是「旅程」（第 1 个义项：从此地到彼地的行程），句意为如果列车准点，这趟要九个钟头。画面里的物件：行李、站台、列车灯。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -er 构成，义为「旅行者」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「旅行」
同源于 jour「日」的形近词，义为「日记；期刊」

senses.title: Travel from one place to another
senses.definition: an act of travelling, especially over a long distance
senses.definitionCN: 一次旅行，尤指长距离的
senses.example: The journey across the mountains took three days.
senses.exampleCN: 翻山那一趟走了三天。
senses.why: The basic sense is simply travel between two named places.
senses.whyCN: 最基本的义项就是两个地名之间的一趟走动。

senses.title: The distance travelled
senses.definition: the length of time or distance covered by travelling
senses.definitionCN: 旅行所花的时间或所走的路程
senses.example: It is a two-hour journey by bus.
senses.exampleCN: 坐公交要两个钟头的路程。
senses.why: The same word names the length of the trip, not only the trip itself.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也指这趟路的长度，而不只是这趟出行。

senses.title: A process of change
senses.definition: a long personal or collective process of growth or change
senses.definitionCN: 个人或集体长期成长与改变的历程
senses.example: Learning the language was a journey of small victories.
senses.exampleCN: 学这门语言是一段由许多小胜利组成的历程。
senses.why: Modern English extended the road image to any long process of change.
senses.whyCN: 现代英语把「路」的意象扩展到任何长期的改变过程。

intro.en: Journey began as French journée, "a day", because travel was measured in days.
intro.cn: journey 起初是法语 journée「一天」，因为旅程是按天来算的。

items.en: diurnus meant "of the day", from dies, "day".
items.cn: diurnus 意为「一天的」，来自 dies「日」。

items.en: journee meant "a day's work or a day's travel".
items.cn: journee 意为「一天的活儿或一天的行程」。

items.en: English took it as journee, still meaning a day's travel.
items.cn: 英语借作 journee，仍指一天的行程。

items.en: The meaning widened from one day to any trip.
items.cn: 词义从「一天」扩到「任何一趟行程」。

items.en: Modern usage adds the inner sense of a process of change.
items.cn: 现代用法又添了「内在历程」这一层。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the journ- stem; the near-meaning group holds words for travelling.
note.cn: 形近组共用 journ- 词干；近义组收表示旅行的词。

entries.definition: A daily record or a magazine.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「日记；期刊」，同词干。

entries.definition: A skilled worker paid by the day.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「熟练工」，原文为按日计酬。

entries.definition: A person who writes for the news.
A short journey for pleasure or business.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「一趟」，多指短程。

entries.definition: A long journey by sea or space.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「航行」，多指海上或太空。

entries.definition: A journey visiting several places.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「游览」，多点巡回。

normalIntro.en: These hooks measure the word in days, as the French did.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子像法国人那样，用「天」来量这个词。

normal.en: jour means day in French.
normal.cn: jour 在法语里是「白天」。

normal.en: A journey was once just a day of travel.
normal.cn: journey 原本只是一天的行程。

normal.en: Longer trips needed more jours, so the meaning grew.
normal.cn: 更长的路要更多「日」，词义就扩大了。

normal.en: A journal is what you write at the end of the day.
normal.cn: journal 是一天结束时写下的东西。

normal.en: Learning is a journey without a station.
normal.cn: 学习是一趟没有站台的旅程。

abstract.en: A journey is a straight line bent by weather.
abstract.cn: 旅程是一条被天气弄弯的直线。

abstract.en: The road is measured in days, the change in years.
abstract.cn: 路用天来量，改变用年来量。

abstract.en: Some journeys end where the traveller begins.
abstract.cn: 有些旅程的终点，正是出发时的自己。

examples.en: The journey from the coast to the capital takes a whole day.
examples.cn: 从海边到首都这一趟要一整天。

examples.en: She kept a notebook of every journey she took.
examples.cn: 她每一趟出行都记在一个本子上。

examples.en: His journey from factory worker to teacher took ten years.
examples.cn: 他从工人到教师的这条路走了十年。

dict_mnemonic.text: jour（日）+ ney —— 一段按日子数的路

root: 拉丁语 dies「日」→ diurnus「一日的」→ 古法语 journee「一天的行程」→ 中古英语 journee → 现代英语 journey。同族有 journal、journeyman、journalist。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: travelling somewhere, the distance covered, and a long inner process.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：出门远行、所走的路程，以及长期的成长历程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road starting at the horizon and going out of sight.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条从地平线起、伸到看不见尽头的路。

branches.en: THE PLATFORM: bags waiting for the departure.
branches.cn: 站台这条线：等着出发的行李。

branches.en: THE MILEAGE: the hours and miles the trip costs.
branches.cn: 里程这条线：这一趟花掉的时间与里数。

branches.en: THE CHANGE: an inner road from one self to another.
branches.cn: 改变这条线：从旧的自己走到新的自己。

branches.en: THE CLOCK: both senses count the trip in time.
branches.cn: 时钟这条线：两个义项都用时间来数一趟路。

branches.en: THE PATIENCE: distance and growth both take days.
branches.cn: 耐心这条线：路程与成长都要一天一天来。

intro.en: Journey is borrowed from French with its day-root jour- intact.
intro.cn: journey 从法语整词借来，含「日」的词根 jour- 完好保留。

latinIntro.en: Latin dies and diurnus stand behind the French word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dies 与 diurnus 藏在法语词背后。

items.example: The root also appears in journal.

items.exampleCN: 它标出「一整天」这段长度。
英语把 journee 改成 journey。
同一个月「日」的词根，写了下来。

definition_zh: 迅速地；急剧地；接连不断地
definition_en: at great speed; within a short time and to a great degree; one after another in quick succession
core_image: 秒针绕着表盘飞速转圈
scene: 仪表盘上的指针一格接一格地跳动，数字不断向上翻。 Prices rose rapidly during the shortage.
sceneCN: 这里 rapidly 是「迅速地」（第 1 个义项：以极快的速度）；句意为短缺期间物价迅速上涨。画面里可留意：跳动的指针、不断上翻的数字。

pos.zh: 迅速地；急剧地；接连不断地

derivatives.zh: rapidly 去掉 -ly，指迅速的
rapid 加 -ity，指迅速、快捷
rapid 加 -s，指河中湍急的一段
rapid 加 -ness，指迅速的状态

senses.title: At great speed
senses.definition: at great speed, of movement or action
senses.definitionCN: 移动或行动以极快的速度
senses.example: Prices rose rapidly during the shortage.
senses.exampleCN: 短缺期间物价迅速上涨。
senses.why: Rapidly is rapid plus the adverb ending, so it describes an action done with the speed that rapid names.
senses.whyCN: rapidly 是 rapid 加副词词尾，因此它描述以 rapid 所指的那种速度完成的动作。

senses.title: Sharply in a short time
senses.definition: suddenly and to a great degree within a short time
senses.definitionCN: 在短时间内突然而大幅度地
senses.example: The situation changed rapidly after the announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 公告发布后局势急剧变化。
senses.why: Because rapid also means sudden in degree, the adverb can describe change that is sharp as well as fast.
senses.whyCN: 由于 rapid 也指幅度上的突然，这个副词既能描述快，也能描述变得剧烈。

senses.title: One after another
senses.definition: in quick succession, with little pause between events
senses.definitionCN: 一个接一个，事件之间几乎没有停顿
senses.example: Reports came rapidly, one after another.
senses.exampleCN: 报告接连不断地传来。
senses.why: When things follow at great speed, the adverb marks not one fast act but a stream of them in quick succession.
senses.whyCN: 当事物以极快速度接连而来，这个副词标记的不是一个快动作，而是一连串紧接的动作。

intro.en: Rapidly is rapid with the English adverb ending -ly, and rapid itself goes back to Latin rapere, to seize and carry away.
intro.cn: rapidly 是 rapid 加上英语副词词尾 -ly，而 rapid 本身可追溯到拉丁语 rapere（抓住并带走）。

items.en: Rapere meant to seize and carry off, the picture behind all forms of this family.
items.cn: rapere 意为抓住并带走，是整个词族背后的画面。

items.en: Rapidus described what is carried along swiftly, and English borrowed it as rapid.
items.cn: rapidus 形容被迅速带走之物，英语把它借作 rapid。

items.en: English kept rapid as an adjective of speed before any adverb was formed from it.
items.cn: 英语先把 rapid 作为表示速度的形容词保留下来，之后才由它构成副词。

items.en: The old English ending -lice became -ly, which turns an adjective into an adverb of manner.
items.cn: 古英语词尾 -lice 演变为 -ly，把形容词变成方式副词。

items.en: Modern English uses rapidly for speed, for sharp change, and for events that follow in quick succession.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rapidly 表示速度、急剧变化，以及紧接而来的事件。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the base word and its close forms; the near-meaning group gathers common adverbs of speed.
note.cn: 形近组收本词的原形与近形；近义组收常用的速度副词。

entries.definition: Very fast.
The quality of being rapid.
Fast, rough water in a river.
The state of being rapid.
At a fast rate.
Fast and smoothly.
With speed, without delay.
At high speed.

normalIntro.en: The adverb adds manner to the adjective rapid, so it tells how fast an action is done, how sharp a change is, or how closely events follow.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词给形容词 rapid 加上「方式」，说明动作做得多快、变化多剧烈，或事件跟得多紧。

normal.en: Rapidly is simply rapid with the adverb ending -ly.
normal.cn: rapidly 就是 rapid 加上副词词尾 -ly。

normal.en: Rapidly and quickly both mean at speed, but rapidly sounds more formal and more forceful.
normal.cn: rapidly 与 quickly 都表示快速，但 rapidly 更正式、更有力。

normal.en: Prices that rise rapidly climb a long way in a short time.
normal.cn: rise rapidly 的物价在短时间内涨了很多。

normal.en: Events that follow rapidly come one after another without pause.
normal.cn: follow rapidly 的事件一个接一个，没有停顿。

normal.en: The root rapere, to seize, is still visible in the force of rapidly.
normal.cn: 词根 rapere（抓住）在 rapidly 的力量感里仍然看得见。

abstract.en: Rapidly measures not distance but the rate at which time is filled.
abstract.cn: rapidly 衡量的不是距离，而是时间被填满的速率。

abstract.en: What happens rapidly often outruns our ability to react.
abstract.cn: 发生得 rapidly 的事，常常快过我们反应的能力。

abstract.en: To change rapidly is to move faster than the old shape can hold.
abstract.cn: 变化 rapidly，就是动得比旧形态所能容纳的更快。

examples.en: The situation changed rapidly after the announcement.
examples.cn: 公告发布后局势迅速变化。

examples.en: The disease spread rapidly through the crowded camp.
examples.cn: 疾病在拥挤的营地中迅速传播。

examples.en: Reports came rapidly, one after another.
examples.cn: 报告接连不断地传来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「表针飞转」——指针一圈圈飞快地转，记住 rapidly 是迅速地。

root: 拉丁语 rapere → rapidus → 英语 rapid + 副词后缀 -ly → rapidly；同族有 rapid、rapidity、rapids。

sensesIntro.en: The core is speed in action; the senses divide into plain speed, sharp change in a short time, and events following one another closely.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是动作中的速度；义项分为单纯的速度、短时间内的急剧变化，以及紧接而来的事件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clock hand spinning round the dial, faster than the eye can follow.
core.cn: 核心意象：钟表指针绕表盘飞转，快得眼睛跟不上。

branches.en: a clock hand spinning fast
branches.cn: 飞速旋转的钟表指针

branches.en: a steeply rising graph
branches.cn: 陡直上升的图表

branches.en: a row of lights flashing in turn
branches.cn: 依次闪亮的一排灯

branches.en: speed and suddenness together
branches.cn: 速度与突然性合在一起

branches.en: sharp change repeated again and again
branches.cn: 反复出现的急剧变化

intro.en: The word is a Latin root with two English layers, the adjective rapid and the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁词根加两层英语成分：形容词 rapid 与副词词尾 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin gives the root: rapere, to seize, and rapidus, carried swiftly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语给出词根：rapere（抓住）与 rapidus（被迅速带走）。

definition_zh: 蜡烛；烛状物
definition_en: a stick of wax with a string through the middle that is burned to give light
core_image: 一支点燃的蜡烛，火苗在黑暗里轻轻摇晃
scene: 停电的那个晚上，妹妹点燃了一支蜡烛，小小的火光把房间照亮。 When the lights went out, my little sister lit a candle in the dark room.
sceneCN: 这里 candle 是「蜡烛」（第 1 个义项：用蜡做成、点燃照明的细长物）；句意为停电的晚上，妹妹点燃蜡烛照亮房间。

collocations.phrase: burn the candle at both ends
collocations.zh: 过度消耗精力；两头燃烧

derivatives.zh: 由 candle 加 light 构成，义为「烛光」
历史上指做蜡烛或卖蜡烛的商人，今多指船具商

senses.title: A wax stick that burns for light
senses.definition: a cylinder of wax with a wick inside that gives light when burned
senses.definitionCN: 中间有烛芯、点燃后发光的蜡制圆柱
senses.example: Grandma put a candle on my birthday cake.
senses.exampleCN: 奶奶在我生日蛋糕上放了一支蜡烛。
senses.why: Fire in a wax stick is a simple, ancient way to make light, so the object is named directly by what it does.
senses.whyCN: 一根蜡里装上火芯就能发光，这是最古老简单的照明方式，词便按用途直接命名。

senses.title: Anything shaped like a candle
senses.definition: an object shaped like a candle, such as a wax roll or a column of rock
senses.definitionCN: 形状像蜡烛的东西，如蜡卷或钟乳石柱
senses.example: Stalactites hang from the cave roof like giant candles.
senses.exampleCN: 钟乳石从洞顶垂下，像巨大的蜡烛。
senses.why: Things that share the shape of a candle borrow its name by likeness.
senses.whyCN: 凡外形与蜡烛相似的物体，都可借它的名字来称呼。

intro.en: Candle comes from a Latin word for something white and shining, carried into English through Old English.
intro.cn: candle 来自拉丁语中指「白色发亮之物」的词，经古英语进入英文。

items.en: Latin candela meant a light or torch, built on candere, to shine white.
items.cn: 拉丁语 candela 指灯或火把，词根 candere 意为发白光。

items.en: Old English took the word as candel for a wax light.
items.cn: 古英语借入为 candel，指蜡制灯火。

items.en: In Middle English the spelling settled as candle and the church candle became common.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写定型为 candle，教堂用烛十分普遍。

items.en: German Kerze shows the same borrowed root in another Germanic tongue.
items.cn: 德语 Kerze 显示同一拉丁词根在另一日耳曼语中的影子。

items.en: Today candle names real wax lights and anything shaped like them.
items.cn: 今天 candle 既指真正的蜡烛，也指一切烛状物。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects other light sources.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收其他光源类词。

entries.definition: The part of a door or tool that you hold.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「把手」，拼写与 candle 接近。

entries.definition: Tiny grains of rock.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「沙子」，读音与 candle 词首接近。

entries.definition: To start a fire burning.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「点燃；激起」，拼写与 candle 相近。

entries.definition: A device that uses oil or electricity to give light.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「灯」，与蜡烛同为照明物。

entries.definition: A stick that burns at one end to light the way.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「火把」，是更古老的照明工具。

entries.definition: A case that protects a light from wind.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「灯笼」，用来护住火光。

normalIntro.en: Remember candle by its root and family.
normalIntro.cn: 借助词根与词族记忆 candle。

normal.en: cand- means shine white, so a candle is a little shining stick.
normal.cn: 词根 cand- 表示「发白光」，candle 就是发光的小棒。

normal.en: candlelight is the light a candle makes.
normal.cn: candlelight 即烛光，两个词直接拼合。

normal.en: blow out the candle on your birthday cake is a fixed scene.
normal.cn: 生日蛋糕上吹蜡烛是固定场景。

normal.en: chandler was once the candle seller.
normal.cn: chandler 旧时指卖蜡烛的商人。

normal.en: kindle and candle share the feeling of starting a flame.
normal.cn: kindle 与 candle 都与点火的感觉相关。

abstract.en: Picture one small flame pushing back the whole dark room.
abstract.cn: 想象一小簇火苗顶开整个黑暗的房间。

abstract.en: Hear the wick crackle softly in the quiet night.
abstract.cn: 静夜里仿佛听见烛芯轻轻的噼啪声。

abstract.en: Feel the warm wax slowly dripping down the side.
abstract.cn: 感受温热的蜡油沿烛身缓缓滑落。

examples.en: The room was dark, so she lit a candle.
examples.cn: 房间很暗，于是她点了一支蜡烛。

examples.en: He blew out the candles and made a wish.
examples.cn: 他吹灭蜡烛许了一个愿。

examples.en: Stalactites in the cave look like giant candles.
examples.cn: 洞里的钟乳石看起来像巨大的蜡烛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坎得儿」——坎上点得儿一支蜡烛，照亮小屋。

root: 拉丁语 candere（发白光）→ candela（灯火）→ 古英语 candel → 现代英语 candle；同根词有 candid（坦白的）、incandescent（白热的）。

sensesIntro.en: Candle moves from the wax light itself to anything shaped like it.
sensesIntro.cn: candle 由真实的蜡烛扩展到一切形似蜡烛之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small flame standing in the dark
core.cn: 核心意象：黑暗中挺立的一小簇火光

branches.en: The burning wax stick
branches.cn: 点燃的蜡棒本体

branches.en: Anything candle-shaped
branches.cn: 一切烛状的东西

branches.en: Light in a power cut
branches.cn: 停电时的光源

branches.en: Birthday and festival scenes
branches.cn: 生日与节日的场景道具

branches.en: Rock columns in caves
branches.cn: 洞穴里的石柱

intro.en: Candle shows the Latin shining root cand- inside an everyday object.
intro.cn: candle 的词身藏着拉丁语「发光」词根 cand-。

latinIntro.en: The root candere, to glow white, lives on in several English words.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 candere（发白光）保留在多个英语词中。

items.meaning: honest and open, shining white in old use
items.meaningCN: 坦白的（旧义为洁白明亮）

items.example: An incandescent bulb lit the hall.

items.meaning: old word for a candle maker
items.example: The chandler sold wax by the pound.
Silver candelabra stood on the table.

definition_zh: 能力；才能；本领；才智
definition_en: the power or skill needed to do something
core_image: 孩子第一次自己骑上自行车
scene: 操场上，一个孩子第一次自己骑上自行车。 Her ability to ride alone surprised the class.
sceneCN: 这里 ability 是「能力」（第 1 个义项：做事的力量或本领）；句意为她独自骑车的能力让全班惊讶。

pos.zh: 名词：能力；才能；本领；才智

derivatives.zh: 能够的；有能力的
能干地；巧妙地
使能够

senses.title: Power to do something
senses.definition: the power or skill needed to do something
senses.definitionCN: 做成某事所需的力量或本领
senses.example: She has the ability to solve hard problems.
senses.exampleCN: 她有解决难题的能力。
senses.why: The noun is built on able, so it names the state of being able to do something.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词由 able 构成，直接表示「能够做成事」的状态。

senses.title: A special talent
senses.definition: a particular skill that stands out in one field
senses.definitionCN: 在某一方面特别突出的本领
senses.example: He showed great ability in music.
senses.exampleCN: 他在音乐上表现出很强的才能。
senses.why: The general power narrows to one field, and that gives the sense of a special talent.
senses.whyCN: 把整体的能力缩小到某一方面，就成了特别突出的才能。

senses.title: A measured level of mind
senses.definition: the level of mental power a person has, seen in comparison
senses.definitionCN: 把不同人的才智放在一起比较所得的水平
senses.example: The test is for students of all abilities.
senses.exampleCN: 这项测试面向各种才智水平的学生。
senses.why: When ability is compared across people, it becomes a level rather than a single power.
senses.whyCN: 当能力被放到不同人之间比较，它就从单一力量变成一种水平。

intro.en: The recorded history of ability is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 ability 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Habilis meant handy or fit, and it described what could do a task well.
items.cn: habilis 意为灵巧、合适，形容能做好某件事。

items.en: Habilitas named the quality of being fit for a task.
items.cn: habilitas 指适合做某事的性质。

items.en: Old French carried the word toward its English shape.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词带向英语的形态。

items.en: English used ability for power of body or mind.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪用 ability 指身体或心智的力量。

items.en: Today it also covers school results and special skills.
items.cn: 今天它也涵盖学业成绩与特殊技能。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: More than one power or skill.
The adjective meaning having the power to do.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为有力量做某事。

entries.definition: The adverb for doing something in a capable way.
It stresses the power to do a particular job.
entries.definitionCN: 强调完成某项工作的能力。

entries.definition: It stresses something learned through practice.
entries.definitionCN: 强调通过练习学到的本领。

entries.definition: It stresses a natural gift.

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: habilis means able and -ity means the quality: ability is the quality of being able.
normal.cn: habilis 表示有能力的，-ity 表示性质：ability 就是有能力这一性质。

normal.en: The same family also gives able and ably.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 able 与 ably。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase the ability to swim.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「游泳的能力」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of ability in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 ability 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: the power or skill needed to do something.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「能力」时用它。

abstract.en: Picture a child riding a bicycle alone for the first time.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子第一次自己骑上自行车。

abstract.en: The same picture can be literal in one sentence and figurative in another.
abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

examples.en: She has the ability to solve hard problems.
examples.cn: 她有解决难题的能力。

examples.en: He showed great ability in music.
examples.cn: 他在音乐上表现出很强的才能。

examples.en: The test is for students of all abilities.
examples.cn: 这项测试面向各种才智水平的学生。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿比勒提」——孩子第一次自己骑车：能力；才能

root: ability 来自拉丁语 habilitas「能力」，由 habilis「有能力的」加 -ity 构成，经古法语进入英语；英语用它指做事的力量、学来的技能与天生的才能，也用于学业与心智能力的测量。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of ability grows from one core image: a child riding a bicycle alone for the first time.
sensesIntro.cn: ability 的各个义项都从同一个核心意象生长出来：孩子第一次自己骑上自行车。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child riding a bicycle alone for the first time
core.cn: 核心意象：孩子第一次自己骑上自行车

branches.en: Sense 01 covers the most literal use: Power to do something.
branches.cn: 义项 01 覆盖最字面的用法：做事的能力。

branches.en: Sense 02 covers a wider everyday use: A special talent.
branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更宽泛的日常用法：某方面的才能。

branches.en: Sense 03 covers a further use: A measured level of mind.
branches.cn: 义项 03 覆盖更靠后的一种用法：才智水平。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 02 covers the two main uses: Power to do something / A special talent.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 02 覆盖两个主要用法：做事的能力、某方面的才能。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 03 covers the two main uses: Power to do something / A measured level of mind.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 03 覆盖两个主要用法：做事的能力、才智水平。

intro.en: ability can be split into the parts below, which also connect it to common English patterns.
intro.cn: ability 可以按下面的成分拆开，这些成分也把它与常见的英语构词方式连起来。

latinIntro.en: No recorded Latin cognate is securely attached to this word, so the list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠记录的拉丁同族词可以系在这个词上，因此该列表留空。

items.exampleCN: 它来自 habilis，意为适合做某事。

items.example: It forms abstract nouns of quality.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表性质的抽象名词。

items.example: It marks a plural noun in English.
It marks the past tense or a completed state.
items.exampleCN: 它标记过去时或已完成的状态。

items.example: It forms the present participle of a verb.
items.exampleCN: 它构成动词的现在分词。

items.example: It turns an adjective into an adverb.
It names the doer of an action.
items.exampleCN: 它指做某动作的人或物。

items.example: It turns an adjective into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成表状态的名词。

definition_zh: 一对；夫妇；情侣；两三个
definition_en: two people or things together, especially two people in love; a small number
core_image: 两个连在一起的东西，像并排的椅子
scene: 公园里，一对老夫妇手牵手慢慢散步，有说有笑。 An elderly couple walks in the park every morning.
sceneCN: 这里 couple 是「夫妇；一对」（第 1 个义项：两个人或物成双出现）；句意是一对老夫妇每天早晨在公园散步。

由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「联结；联轴器」

senses.title: Two people together, often in love or married
senses.titleCN: 成双的两个人，常指夫妇或情侣
senses.definition: two people who are together, especially husband and wife or two people in love
senses.definitionCN: 在一起的两个人，尤指夫妻或恋人
senses.example: The young couple took photos before the old school gate.
senses.exampleCN: 这对年轻情侣在校门前拍了照。
senses.why: The core image is two joined as one unit, so two people who act as one get called a couple.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是两个连成一个整体，所以像一体一样行动的两个人就被称为 a couple。

senses.title: A small number, two or a few
senses.definition: a small number of things or people, more than one but not many
senses.definitionCN: 数量不多，不止一个但也不多
senses.example: Give me a couple of minutes to find my key.
senses.exampleCN: 给我两分钟找钥匙。
senses.why: When two became the common way to say a handful, the word stretched to mean any few.
senses.whyCN: 当「两个」成为表示「一小把」的常用说法后，这个词就扩展成指任意少数几个。

senses.title: To join two things together
senses.definition: to fasten or connect two things so they work together
senses.definitionCN: 把两个东西连接或搭配起来，使它们协同工作
senses.example: The teacher coupled each player with a younger partner.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把每个队员和一名低年级同学配对。
senses.why: Joining two into one pair is the action behind the noun, so the verb simply means to make a pair.
senses.whyCN: 把两个合成一对正是名词背后的动作，所以动词义就是「配成对」。

intro.en: Couple descends from a Latin word for a bond or tie.
intro.cn: couple 源自一个表示「束缚、联结」的拉丁词。

items.en: The Latin copula meant a bond or tie, from co- (together) + apere (to fasten).
items.cn: 拉丁语 copula 意为联结、纽带，由 co-（一起）+ apere（系紧）构成。

items.en: Old French made cople, meaning a pair joined together.
items.cn: 古法语形成 cople，指联结成对的一组。

items.en: English borrowed cople in the thirteenth century for two joined things.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 cople，指连在一起的两个东西。

items.en: It soon meant two people married or in love, and loosely a few.
items.cn: 它很快指结婚或相爱的两个人，也泛指少数几个。

items.en: The verb to couple keeps the original idea of fastening two together.
items.cn: 动词 to couple 保留了把两者系在一起的原始意思。

note.en: These words mean pairs or small numbers, or look alike.
note.cn: 这些词表示成对或少量，或与 couple 拼写相近。

normalIntro.en: Use the pair idea and a couple of easy phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 用「成对」的概念和几个简单短语来记。

normal.en: couple = co + ple: pulled together into one pair.
normal.cn: couple = co（一起）+ ple（系）：被拉到一起成为一对。

normal.en: a couple of = two or a few, never a huge number.
normal.cn: a couple of ＝两个或几个，绝不是很大数目。

normal.en: Married couple is the most common phrase in daily talk.
normal.cn: married couple 是日常口语里最常见的说法。

normal.en: The verb couples things the way the noun pairs them.
normal.cn: 动词 couple 把东西配起来，正如名词把它们成对。

normal.en: Couplet keeps a tiny -et, meaning a small pair of lines.
normal.cn: couplet 带个小后缀 -et，指小小的一对诗行。

abstract.en: See two seats screwed side by side; that join is the core image.
abstract.cn: 想象两把椅子并排固定，那个连接就是核心意象。

abstract.en: Two hands clasped in a wedding photo: one couple, one unit.
abstract.cn: 婚礼照上交握的两只手：一对夫妇，一个整体。

abstract.en: Hold up two fingers, then relax the count; that is a couple of minutes.
abstract.cn: 竖起两根手指再把数放松些，这就是 a couple of minutes。

examples.en: The couple next door has two lovely cats.
examples.cn: 隔壁那对夫妇养了两只可爱的猫。

examples.en: Wait a couple of seconds before the light turns green.
examples.cn: 等个两三秒再等灯变绿。

examples.en: The trailer was coupled to the car in seconds.
examples.cn: 拖车几秒钟就连接到了汽车上。

sensesIntro.cn: 从成双的人，到少数几个，再到连接这个动作。

definition_en: the act of showing thoughts or feelings, or the look on a face that shows them
core_image: 心里的东西被一股力量压出来，落在脸上、纸上或公式里
scene: 她听到消息后没有说话，脸上的神情却先变了，同事低声说： Her expression changed before she found the words.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「脸上显示情绪的神情」（第 2 个义项：面部神情）；句意为她还没找到话说，神情就先变了。

senses.title: The act of showing thoughts or feelings
senses.titleCN: 把想法或情感表达出来的行为
senses.definition: the act of making thoughts, feelings or ideas known
senses.definitionCN: 把想法、情感或观点让人知道的行为
senses.example: Freedom of expression is protected by law.
senses.exampleCN: 表达自由受法律保护。
senses.why: The core image is pressing something inward out into the open, and the first sense is simply that outward movement.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是把里面的东西压到外面来，第 1 个义项就是这一向外的动作本身。

senses.title: The look on a face
senses.definition: the appearance of a person's face that shows a feeling or state of mind
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的脸部外观所显示的情绪或心理状态
senses.example: His expression softened when he heard the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到这个消息，他的神情柔和下来。
senses.why: The face is the most visible surface where inner feeling is pressed into public view.
senses.whyCN: 脸是内心情感被压到公众视野里最显眼的表面。

senses.title: A word or phrase
senses.definition: a particular word, phrase or way of saying something
senses.definitionCN: 某个特定的词、短语或说法
senses.example: A local expression puzzled the translator.
senses.exampleCN: 一个当地说法让译者困惑。
senses.why: A fixed group of words is a small package into which a meaning has already been pressed.
senses.whyCN: 一组固定的词就像一个小包裹，意义早已被压进其中。

senses.title: Vivid delivery in speech or music
senses.titleCN: 说话或演奏时的表现力
senses.definition: the quality of conveying feeling through voice, phrasing or performance
senses.definitionCN: 通过嗓音、措辞或表演传达情感的特质
senses.example: She read the poem with great expression.
senses.exampleCN: 她极富表现力地朗读了这首诗。
senses.why: Once the outward push is done with skill, the delivery itself becomes noticeable and can be praised.
senses.whyCN: 当向外的推送带有技巧时，表达方式本身就会变得显眼并值得称赞。

senses.title: A mathematical expression
senses.definition: a combination of numbers, symbols and operations that stands for a value
senses.definitionCN: 由数字、符号与运算组成、代表某个值的组合
senses.example: Simplify the expression before substituting values.
senses.exampleCN: 先化简表达式，再代入数值。
senses.why: Mathematics writes a value as a visible string of symbols, pressing an abstract quantity into a readable form.
senses.whyCN: 数学把一个值写成可见的符号串，把抽象量压成可读的形式。

senses.title: Gene expression in biology
senses.definition: the process by which information in a gene is turned into a working product
senses.definitionCN: 基因中的信息被转成可用产物的过程
senses.example: The gene's expression rises under heat stress.
senses.exampleCN: 在热应激下，这个基因的表达增强。
senses.why: A gene carries hidden instructions, and expression is the moment those instructions are pushed out into the cell.
senses.whyCN: 基因携带隐藏的指令，表达就是这些指令被推到细胞里发挥作用的时刻。

senses.title: Pressing out juice or oil
senses.definition: the physical act of squeezing liquid out of fruit, seeds or peel
senses.definitionCN: 从果实、种子或果皮中挤出液体的物理动作
senses.example: Cold expression of the peel releases the essential oil.
senses.exampleCN: 冷榨果皮能释放出精油。
senses.why: This is the oldest concrete sense: the word's root literally means to press out, and liquids are pressed from plants.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的具体义：词根字面就是「压出来」，而液体正是从植物中被压出的。

senses.title: A manifestation or sign
senses.titleCN: 某种态度或品质的显现
senses.definition: an act or thing that shows a quality, attitude or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 显示某种品质、态度或情感的行为或事物
senses.example: The grant is an expression of confidence in the team.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔资助是对该团队信心的体现。
senses.why: The abstract sense generalizes the push: an inner attitude becomes visible through an outer act.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把「推送」一般化：内在态度通过外在行为变得可见。

intro.en: Expression comes through Old French from Latin expressio, a noun of action from exprimere 'to press out', built on ex- 'out' and premere 'to press'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: expression 经古法语来自拉丁语 expressio，这是动词 exprimere「压出」的行为名词，由拉丁语表示「向外」的前缀与 premere「压」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Premere meant 'to press'. Its deeper origin is not established, and the Indo-European root sometimes proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: premere 意为「压」。其更深来源未得到证明，有人为它提出的印欧词根只是重构形式。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus premere produced exprimere 'to press out, squeeze out'; it also developed the sense 'to represent or portray'.
items.cn: 表示「向外」的拉丁前缀加 premere 构成 exprimere「压出、挤出」；它还发展出「表现、描绘」的意义。

items.en: The action noun expressio named both a physical pressing out and a representation in words or art.
items.cn: 行为名词 expressio 既指物理上的压出，也指用词语或艺术的表现。

items.en: Old French expression entered English in the fourteenth century, first as the act of expressing and as an utterance.
items.cn: 古法语 expression 在十四世纪进入英语，最初指表达的行为与说出的话。

items.en: The facial sense took shape in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, while algebra adopted the word for a symbolic string and biology adopted it for gene activity in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 面部义在十七至十八世纪成形；代数学采用这个词指符号串，生物学则在二十世纪用它指基因活动。

items.en: Source uncertain: the date of the facial sense is not exact, and the pre-Latin origin of premere remains unsettled, so every proposed root form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：面部义的确切年代不确定，premere 在拉丁语之前的来源也仍未确定，因此提出的各种词根形式都属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words built with the same pressing root but different prefixes; group two holds near neighbours in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「压」这一词根、但前缀不同的词；第二组是语义相近的词。

entries.definition: Built with 'in' rather than 'out': something presses into the mind and leaves an impression, not an outward expression.
entries.definitionCN: 用的是「向内」而非「向外」的前缀：某物压进心里留下印象，而不是向外的表达。

entries.definition: The prefix means 'together': it names pressing something into a smaller space, with no idea of showing meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀意为「共同」：指把某物压进更小的空间，与显示意义无关。

entries.definition: The prefix means 'under': it names holding something down or stopping it, often feelings or information.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀意为「在下」：指把某物压住或制止，常指情感或信息。

entries.definition: It looks as if it should belong to the pressing family, but its root means 'to appease or atone', not 'to press'.
entries.definitionCN: 看起来像属于「压」这个词族，其实词根意为「安抚、赎罪」，并非「压」。

entries.definition: A plain word for the appearance of a face; expression adds the idea that the look reveals inner feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 指脸部外观的朴素词；expression 多了「神情显示内心情感」这一层。

entries.definition: A group of words forming a unit; expression can also mean a fixed saying, but it is broader and more idiomatic.
entries.definitionCN: 构成一个单位的词组；expression 也可指固定说法，但范围更宽、更习语化。

entries.definition: A technical term for a unit of speech; expression points more to the meaning being conveyed than to the sound produced.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个言语单位的技术术语；expression 更指向被传达的意义，而不是发出的声音。

entries.definition: A formal word for something that makes an inner quality visible, close to the eighth sense of expression.
entries.definitionCN: 指使内在品质变得可见的正式用词，接近 expression 的第 8 个义项。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the pressing root, the prefix contrasts and the real technical uses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示「压」的词根、前缀对比与真实的技术用法。

normal.en: The root means 'press', so expression is a pressing outward of what was inside.
normal.cn: 词根意为「压」，因此这个词就是把里面的东西向外压出来。

normal.en: Prefix contrast: outward pressing gives expression, inward pressing gives impression.
normal.cn: 前缀对比：向外压得到「表达」，向内压得到「印象」。

normal.en: Face use: the same word names the look that shows feeling.
normal.cn: 面部用法：同一个词也命名显示情感的神情。

normal.en: Technical spread: algebra uses it for a symbolic string, biology for gene activity.
normal.cn: 技术延伸：代数学用它指符号串，生物学用它指基因活动。

normal.en: Everyday phrase: freedom of expression names the right to make ideas public.
normal.cn: 日常搭配：表达自由指把想法公开的权利。

abstract.en: Picture a hand squeezing a fruit until the juice lands in a glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手挤压果子，汁水落进杯子里。

abstract.en: Picture an inner feeling rising to the surface of a face like water to a well.
abstract.cn: 想象内心的情感升到脸的表面，像水升到井口。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence folded into a small box that can be handed to someone.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话被折进一个小盒子，可以递给别人。

examples.en: The court treated the letter as an expression of intent.
examples.cn: 法院把这封信视为意向的表达。

examples.en: Her expression did not match the cheerful words she used.
examples.cn: 她的神情与她使用的欢快词语并不一致。

examples.en: The software evaluates each expression before running the program.
examples.cn: 软件在运行程序前先求值每一个表达式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「向外」加「压」——把心里的东西压出来 → 表达、表情

root: 拉丁语 exprimere「压出」= 表示「向外」的前缀 + premere「压」，其行为名词为 expressio；premere 更深来源不确定，相关印欧词根为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one outward push: the act itself, the face that shows it, the phrase that packages it, the delivery, the formula, the gene, the pressed juice and the visible sign.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次向外的推送展开：行为本身、显现在脸上、被包进词语、表现方式、公式、基因、榨出的汁液以及可见的迹象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something inside is pressed outward and becomes visible.
core.cn: 核心意象：里面的东西被向外压出，变得可见。

branches.en: OUTWARD ACT: making an inner state public and letting it appear as a sign are the same push seen at two levels.
branches.cn: 向外的行为：把内在状态公开，与让它显现为迹象，是同一个推送在两个层面上的样子。

branches.en: FACE: the most visible surface on which feeling is pressed into view.
branches.cn: 脸：情感被压到视野里最显眼的表面。

branches.en: PACKAGED WORDS: a fixed phrase is a small box that already holds a meaning.
branches.cn: 被包好的词语：一个固定短语就是一只已经装着意义的小盒子。

branches.en: FORCE AND DELIVERY: the pressure that squeezes oil also shapes the skilled delivery of a line.
branches.cn: 力量与表现：挤压油液的压力，也塑造一句台词的熟练表达。

branches.en: SYMBOLIC AND BIOLOGICAL EXPRESSION: a formula makes a value readable, and a gene makes its instructions active.
branches.cn: 符号与生物表达：公式让数值可读，基因让指令发挥作用。

intro.en: Expression is made of a Latin prefix, a Latin verb root and a noun suffix, and the same parts build a whole family of show-and-press words.
intro.cn: expression 由一个拉丁前缀、一个拉丁动词词根与一个名词后缀构成，同样的部件构成了一整族表示「压出与表现」的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin premere 'to press' and ex- 'out' produce exprimere and its noun expressio; English adds the suffixes that build the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「压」的词根与表示「向外」的前缀构成 exprimere 及其名词 expressio；英语再加上构成词族的后缀。

items.example: The prefix directs the action away from the inside.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作引向外部。

items.example: The root supplies the physical force in the image.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供意象中的物理力量。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a name for its action.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成其行为的名词。

items.example: The expression of grief took the form of silence.
items.exampleCN: 悲伤的表达采取了沉默的形式。

items.meaning: to press out; to say or show
items.example: He expressed his thanks in a short letter.
items.exampleCN: 他用一封短信表达了感谢。

items.example: Her expressive reading held the room.
items.exampleCN: 她富有表现力的朗读抓住了全场。

items.example: His expressionless face gave nothing away.
items.exampleCN: 他面无表情，没有泄露任何信息。

items.meaning: an art movement that distorts form to show feeling
items.meaningCN: 为表现情感而扭曲形式的艺术运动
items.example: Expressionism used violent colour to show inner states.
items.exampleCN: 表现主义用强烈的色彩显示内心状态。

items.example: The expressionist painted faces as blocks of colour.
items.exampleCN: 这位表现主义画家把脸画成色块。
